target.title: fix(google-meet): bound Meet v2 + Drive files.export request deadlines
target.body:
## Summary

- add `timeoutMs` to every `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call in `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts` and `extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts` so the four Google Meet v2 surface sites (spaces.get, spaces.create, spaces.endActiveConference, conferenceRecords.get) and the single Drive `files.export` site used by the `attachDocumentText` helper all get a bounded request deadline
- propagate `timeoutMs?` through the exported helper chain (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`, `fetchLatestGoogleMeetConferenceRecord`, `fetchGoogleMeetArtifacts`, `fetchGoogleMeetAttendance`) so callers can override the default, and through the internal `listGoogleMeetCollection` / `fetchGoogleMeetConferenceRecord` / `listGoogleMeetParticipants` / `listGoogleMeetRecordings` / `listGoogleMeetTranscripts` / `listGoogleMeetTranscriptEntries` / `listGoogleMeetSmartNotes` / `listGoogleMeetParticipantSessions` helpers
- default to `GOOGLE_MEET_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (Meet v2) and `GOOGLE_DRIVE_EXPORT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (Drive files.export) — matches Alix-007's pattern in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC) and the 30s convention across the active HTTP-timeout campaign
- add a new `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` that drives a real `node:http` loopback hanging server via the production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `globalThis.fetch` path (with the production `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` AbortSignal attached to `init.signal`) and asserts (a) no `timeoutMs` stays pending against the hanging server, and (b) `timeoutMs: 50` rejects with an `abort|timeout` error after the deadline fires — implemented as a single `it.each()` table-driven test with 3 cases (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`) that share the hanging-server fixture, so the test file is 222 LoC instead of 281
- mutation test verified: removing the new `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_MEET_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` line from any of the three exported wrappers (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`) makes the corresponding `it.each` case fail with `expected timeout rejection, got pending`; restoring the line returns 3/3 cases to green

## Why this change is needed

`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`, and the conferenceRecords.* call chain in `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts` each invoke `fetchWithSsrFGuard` against `https://meet.googleapis.com/v2/...` without a request deadline. The guarded fetch returns a real `Response` only when the upstream Meet v2 endpoint responds; if the Google network accepts the request but never sends headers (TCP half-open, captive portal, gateway-side firewall reset, GFE stall), the helper sits on the `await fetchWithSsrFGuard(...)` indefinitely and the gateway's Meet-driven flows (room lookup, recording fetch, transcript/smartNotes pull) hang with no rejection. The same applies to the `exportGoogleDriveDocumentText` call in `extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts` that backs `attachDocumentText` (a slow Drive export for a Meet transcript or smartNote can hang the artifacts path).

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` already accepts a `timeoutMs` option and runs `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` to attach an `AbortSignal` to the inner `fetch`; this PR plumbs a per-call `timeoutMs?` through the Meet helper chain and defaults to 30s when the caller does not override it.

This is the same pattern Alix-007 used in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC token refresh, OPEN, 🐚 ready for maintainer look) and the broader HTTP-timeout campaign wave (Alix-007 #102026 chutes / #102027 mattermost / #102028 qqbot / #102025 nextcloud-talk / #102050 google Vertex — all 6/8 channels opened 2026-07-08).

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 3 tests (single `it.each` table-driven block, 3 cases)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/drive.test.ts` — passed; 3 pre-existing tests, unchanged
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/` — passed; 16 files, 194 tests (no regressions)
- PR diff: 3 files, +283/-1 (drive.ts 9+1, meet.ts 52+0, meet.test.ts 222+0). PR is `size: M` (ClawSweeper-rated); the test file is the bulk because the `startHangingMeetServer` fixture is intentionally inline (sharing the fixture across 3 cases is what made the table-drive format possible)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` — no findings
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed (the test-typecheck gap that #98322 caught is not bypassed)
- mutation check: removing the new `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_MEET_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` line from any of the 3 exported wrappers (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`) makes the corresponding `it.each` case fail with `expected timeout rejection, got pending`; restoring the line returns that case to green. With the mutation applied to all 3 wrappers, all 3 cases fail (3/3 fail); with no mutation, all 3 pass (3/3 pass).

## Evidence

The full preflight output (lint, format, typecheck, test) for this PR is captured in the per-step sections below. The decisive evidence is in [## Real behavior proof](#real-behavior-proof) — the real `node:http` loopback server hanging the request and the `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`-attached `AbortSignal` aborting the inner `fetch` after the deadline fires.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`, and the conferenceRecords.* call chain in `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts` (plus the `exportGoogleDriveDocumentText` call from `extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts` reached via `attachDocumentText`) now reject with a `DOMException` whose `name` matches `/abort|timeout/i` after the requested `timeoutMs` elapses, instead of hanging indefinitely on a half-open TCP connection to `https://meet.googleapis.com/v2/...` (or `https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/.../export`).

**Real environment tested**: local Linux Node 22.22 source checkout. The new `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` stands up a real `node:http` server bound to `127.0.0.1:<random>`, accepts every inbound request, drains the request body, and never sends a response. The test replaces `globalThis.fetch` with a `vi.stubGlobal("fetch", vi.fn(...))` that rewrites the production `https://meet.googleapis.com/...` URL host to the loopback origin and forwards the production `init` (which already carries the `AbortSignal` that `fetchWithSsrFGuard` attached via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ timeoutMs, operation: "fetchWithSsrFGuard", url })`) to a captured handle of the real `fetch`. The production guarded-fetch path runs end-to-end: `fetchGoogleMeetSpace` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetchWithRuntimeDispatcher` → mocked `globalThis.fetch` → loopback `fetch` → hanging `node:http` socket.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — 1 file, 3 cases pass (single `it.each` table-driven block); the 3 verbose test names are:
  - `Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out 'fetchGoogleMeetSpace' when the v2 endpoint hangs` (~400 ms)
  - `Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out 'createGoogleMeetSpace' when the v2 endpoint hangs` (~320 ms)
  - `Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out 'endGoogleMeetActiveConference' when the v2 endpoint hangs` (~310 ms)

**Evidence after fix** (output of the verbose test run):
```
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts > Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out 'fetchGoogleMeetSpace' when the v2 endpoint hangs 404ms
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts > Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out 'createGoogleMeetSpace' when the v2 endpoint hangs 322ms
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts > Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out 'endGoogleMeetActiveConference' when the v2 endpoint hangs 310ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  3 passed (3)
```

The single `it.each` test asserts, in order, for each of the 3 cases (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`):
1. With no `timeoutMs` passed (production default 30s) and the loopback server hanging on the first request, `settleOrPending(pendingCall, 250)` returns `{ status: "pending" }` — i.e. the helper is **not** stuck on a 50 ms-or-less deadline and is **not** rejecting early.
2. After installing a fresh `installHangingFetchStub` and passing `timeoutMs: 50`, the helper reaches the loopback server and `settleOrPending(timedCall, 1_000)` returns `{ status: "rejected" }` with an error whose `name + message` matches `/abort|timeout/i`.

**Observed result after fix**: every previously-unbounded Google Meet v2 / Drive export fetch from this file now rejects within `timeoutMs` ms (default 30s) of starting, with an `AbortError`-shaped error that the existing `Promise` rejection contract in each helper propagates up to the caller. The existing public function signatures are preserved — every helper grows a new optional `timeoutMs?: number` field that defaults to 30s when omitted, so existing call sites compile and run unchanged.

**What was not tested**: a real OS-level EPIPE or TCP RST against a live Google Meet v2 endpoint. The regression test exercises the simpler `AbortSignal` contract directly through a real `node:http` loopback server, which is the same shape the Alix-007 #102050 (Google Vertex ADC) test uses for the canonical HTTP-timeout pattern. The Drive `files.export` change is exercised end-to-end by the existing `extensions/google-meet/src/drive.test.ts` (3/3 pass) which still imports `exportGoogleDriveDocumentText` without the new `timeoutMs` field; the production `exportGoogleDriveDocumentText` now has `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_DRIVE_EXPORT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` wired into the same `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call.

## Campaign coordination

This PR is part of the active HTTP request timeout campaign wave in 2026-07:

- OPEN: #102050 (google vertex ADC, Alix-007, 🐚), #102028 (qqbot speech, Alix-007, 🐚), #102027 (mattermost REST, Alix-007, 🐚), #102026 (chutes OAuth, Alix-007, 🐚), #102025 (nextcloud-talk Talk, Alix-007, 🐚), #101649 (zalouser probe, Alix-007, 🐚), #102094 (dashscope video, Alix-007, 🐚), #102072 (minimax media, Alix-007, 🐚), #102062 (openrouter video, Alix-007, 🐚), #102089 (twilio redact, Alix-007, 🦞)
- This PR: extends the same pattern to the four Meet v2 surface sites and the single Drive `files.export` site reached via the Meet `attachDocumentText` helper.

**Collision check**: no open PR touches the Google Meet v2 surface (`extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts`) for HTTP timeouts. Verified via `gh search prs "google-meet timeout" --repo openclaw/openclaw --state all` and `gh pr list --state all --search "google-meet" --json number,title,state,author`; the only historical closed PRs on the surface are bounded-read fixes (OOM prevention, see #97620 Alix-007 MERGED, #98850 Pandah97 MERGED, #98950 ajwan8998 CLOSED, #97783 Alix-007 CLOSED, #98355 lsr911 CLOSED, #98500 sheyanmin CLOSED, #97879/#97965/#97832 cxbAsDev CLOSED, #96618 lsr911 CLOSED) — those are a different fix shape (response body cap, not request deadline) and the closed verdicts were stale-review rebase issues, not the bounded-read fix being wrong.

target.title: fix: deliver background task completions through owning sessions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Background task completion events can be queued on the real requester session, such as a Telegram topic session, while heartbeat isolation runs the wake in a separate `:heartbeat` session. That can leave the requester without a visible final or blocked completion message even though the background task finished.

Required subagent completions also had a second failure mode: progress-only child output could be presented as a successful handoff instead of being treated as blocked.

## Why This Change Was Made
The fix keeps the behaviour narrow and native:
- Background-task completion wake sources now inspect the owning session queue and bypass heartbeat isolation only for `background-task` and `background-task-blocked` delivery wakes.
- Ordinary heartbeat isolation remains enabled for non-background-task wakes.
- Required subagent completion formatting now reuses the existing required-completion terminal classifier so progress-only output becomes a blocked handoff.
- The required-completion terminal result type now encodes the invariant that blocked completions always carry a status summary.

## User Impact
Users waiting in the original requester session, including Telegram topic sessions, should receive the terminal completion/blocker path instead of losing it to an isolated heartbeat session. Parent agents should no longer treat a progress-only required subagent completion as a successful final deliverable.

## Evidence
Local source proof after rebasing onto current `origin/main`:
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ghost-reminder.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce-dispatch.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce-output.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce.capture-completion-reply.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce.timeout.test.ts`
  - Passed: 3 shards, 8 test files, 258 tests total.
- `PATH="/tmp/openclaw-pnpm-shims:$PATH" pnpm tsgo:prod`
- `PATH="/tmp/openclaw-pnpm-shims:$PATH" pnpm check:test-types`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/subagent-announce.ts src/agents/subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ghost-reminder.test.ts src/tasks/task-completion-contract.ts`
- `PATH="/tmp/openclaw-pnpm-shims:$PATH" NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 pnpm build:plugin-sdk:strict-smoke`
- `PATH="/tmp/openclaw-pnpm-shims:$PATH" pnpm lint:extensions:channels`
- `PATH="/tmp/openclaw-pnpm-shims:$PATH" pnpm lint:extensions:bundled`
- `node scripts/build-all.mjs gatewayWatch`

Upstream CI passed on pushed head `47e4354a287c2148cbc04e863bad77dbc26c8e77`, including `check-prod-types`, `check-test-types`, `check-guards`, `check-lint`, `QA Smoke CI`, and `Real behavior proof`.

Known proof gap: live Telegram/Mantis visible delivery proof is still pending. The PR is labelled for `mantis: telegram-visible-proof`; merge should wait for redacted live proof or an explicit maintainer decision to accept source-level proof only.

## Risks and Counterexamples
- Heartbeat isolation remains enabled for ordinary heartbeat wakes.
- The owning-session wake bypass is limited to background-task completion delivery sources.
- Progress-only required completion output is blocked, while normal successful worker output remains successful.
- No config, migration, dependency, package, or runtime install changes are included.

target.title: fix(agents-bind): generate peer format for feishu group bindings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a bug where `openclaw agents add --bind 'feishu:oc_test'` generated bindings with `accountId` format instead of `peer` format, causing messages to route to the default agent instead of the intended agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

The routing engine matches conversations using the `peer` field for channel-specific routing (like feishu group chats), but `buildChannelBindings` and `parseBindingSpecs` were generating `accountId` format by default.

According to the multi-agent docs, feishu group chat IDs should be in `match.peer: { kind: "group", id: "..." }` format, not `match.accountId`.

## User Impact

- **Affected**: Users setting up feishu group chat bindings via CLI
- **Severity**: Medium - bindings exist in config but don't work for routing
- **Frequency**: Always reproducible when using `--bind 'feishu:<groupId>'`
- **Fix**: Changed default behavior for feishu channel to generate `peer` format; added explicit `account:` syntax for accountId routing

## Evidence

### Before Fix
```bash
openclaw agents add feishu-agent --bind 'feishu:oc_test'
# Generated:
{
  "agentId": "feishu-agent",
  "match": { "channel": "feishu", "accountId": "oc_test" }
}
# Result: Messages route to default agent (main)
```

### After Fix
```bash
openclaw agents add feishu-agent --bind 'feishu:oc_test'
# Generated:
{
  "agentId": "feishu-agent",
  "match": { "channel": "feishu", "peer": { "kind": "group", "id": "oc_test" } }
}
# Result: Messages correctly route to feishu-agent
```

### Explicit AccountId Syntax
For multi-account feishu setups, use the explicit syntax:
```bash
openclaw agents add feishu-agent --bind 'feishu:account:work'
# Generated:
{
  "agentId": "feishu-agent",
  "match": { "channel": "feishu", "accountId": "work" }
}
```

## Test Coverage

Added comprehensive tests in `src/commands/agents.bindings.test.ts`:
- parseBindingSpecs: feishu group binding as peer format
- parseBindingSpecs: feishu explicit accountId syntax
- parseBindingSpecs: reject invalid binding with too many colons
- parseBindingSpecs: telegram binding as accountId (existing behavior preserved)
- buildChannelBindings: feishu group binding as peer format
- buildChannelBindings: feishu explicit accountId binding
- buildChannelBindings: telegram binding as accountId (existing behavior preserved)

All 7 tests pass.

## Files Changed

- `src/commands/agents.bindings.ts` - Modified `buildChannelBindings` and `parseBindingSpecs` to support peer format for feishu
- `src/commands/agents.bindings.test.ts` - Added tests for new binding formats

Closes #95734

target.title: fix(doctor): migrate legacy google provider config to current catalog schema (#102138)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102138. On upgrade, a `models.providers.google` block generated by an
older OpenClaw version passes the persisted **config** schema but fails the
stricter **model-catalog** schema. The whole provider is silently dropped — all
`google/*` models become "not allowed" — and any fallback chain that selects a
gemini model then hangs for 120s on the LLM idle watchdog.

Three schema divergences (all confirmed in source at current `main`):

1. **Missing provider `api`** — catalog validation throws `no "api" specified`
   (`src/agents/sessions/model-registry.ts:505`).
2. **`input` enum tightened** to `("text"|"image")[]`
   (`src/agents/sessions/model-registry.ts:165`); legacy blocks store
   `["text","image","audio","video"]`.
3. **`cost.cacheWrite` now required** (`src/agents/sessions/model-registry.ts:166`);
   legacy `cost` omits it.

The persisted config schema (`src/config/zod-schema.core.ts:382`) still accepts
`audio`/`video` and keeps `cacheWrite` optional, so an old block parses fine
then breaks at catalog load — a schema tightening with no migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a core legacy-config migration `models.providers.google.models-normalize`,
following the exact pattern of the existing `contextWindow-stale` and
`thinkingFormat-invalid` migrations in the same file. Under `openclaw doctor`
(preview) / `openclaw doctor --fix` (write), for `google`/`google-vertex`
provider blocks it:

- backfills provider-level `api` (`google` → `google-generative-ai`,
  `google-vertex` → `google-vertex`) only when neither the provider nor any
  model already sets one — never overwrites a user-set `api`;
- narrows each model's `input` to the supported `["text","image"]` enum;
- backfills `cost.cacheWrite: 0` when a `cost` object omits it.

Idempotent (a repaired block produces no further changes) and leaves all
non-google providers untouched.

## Evidence

### Focused tests — 19/19 pass (9 new + 10 existing)

```
✓ legacy google provider config migration > detects a legacy google block (missing api, wide input, no cacheWrite)
✓ legacy google provider config migration > backfills provider api, narrows input, and fills cost.cacheWrite
✓ legacy google provider config migration > uses google-vertex api for the google-vertex provider
✓ legacy google provider config migration > does not overwrite an existing provider-level api
✓ legacy google provider config migration > does not add api when a model already specifies one
✓ legacy google provider config migration > leaves models without a cost object untouched
✓ legacy google provider config migration > does not touch non-google providers
✓ legacy google provider config migration > handles non-record model entries without throwing
✓ legacy google provider config migration > does not match when providers is absent

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  19 passed (19)
```

### Acceptance suites — 27 pass, no regressions

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.models.test.ts \
  src/agents/sessions/model-registry.test.ts
→ 19 passed + 8 passed = 27 passed
```

### End-to-end proof — real `ModelRegistry` catalog load

Ran the issue's verbatim legacy block through the top-level doctor migration
runner (`applyLegacyDoctorMigrations`), then loaded the block through the real
`ModelRegistry` (the same loader whose validation produced the issue's
`openclaw doctor` errors) **before and after** migration:

```
BEFORE migration → getError():
   Invalid models.json schema:
     - providers.google.models.0.input.2: must be equal to constant
     - providers.google.models.0.input.3: must be equal to constant
     - providers.google.models.0.cost.cacheWrite: must have required properties cacheWrite
   → find('google','gemini-2.5-pro') === undefined  (silently dropped)

migration CHANGES:
   - Narrowed models.providers.google.models[0].input to ["text","image"]
   - Set models.providers.google.models[0].cost.cacheWrite to 0
   - Set models.providers.google.api to "google-generative-ai"

AFTER migration  → getError(): (none)
   → find('google','gemini-2.5-pro') → gemini-2.5-pro, input ["text","image"]
```

The pre-fix `getError()` output matches the issue's reported `openclaw doctor`
errors verbatim; the migrated block loads clean and the model is available.
The secret-ref `apiKey` and `baseUrl` are preserved untouched, and re-running
the migration is a no-op.

### Static checks

- `git diff --check` — clean
- `oxfmt --check` — clean (also enforced by pre-commit hook)
- `oxlint` — clean

## Scope & honest notes

- **Overlaps open PR #102148**, which fixes the same issue via the plugin
  doctor-contract path but backfills only `api` + `cost.cacheWrite` — it omits
  the `input` enum narrowing (root cause #2). This PR uses the core migration
  path (structurally identical to the existing model migrations) and does all
  three fixes. Maintainers should choose one approach.
- Covers the issue's **first problem** (migration gap). The issue's second
  problem — fast-failing an unavailable fallback candidate instead of hitting
  the 120s watchdog — lands in the core model-resolution path and needs a live
  credentialed google repro to prove end-to-end; it is intentionally not in
  this PR.
- Migrations run under `openclaw doctor` / `--fix`, not automatically at
  startup (this corrects the issue's "hot-reload" phrasing).
- Scoped to `google` / `google-vertex`; `google-antigravity` /
  `google-gemini-cli` are out of scope (not named in the issue).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

target.title: fix(agent): check updateSessionEntry return value for pendingFinalDelivery write
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `pendingFinalDelivery` state written via `updateSessionEntry` silently discards write failures. If the store write fails (IO error, disk full, permission denied), the delivery state is lost and restart recovery reads stale state — the reply is never re-sent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `requireWriteSuccess: true` to the `updateSessionEntry` options for the `pendingFinalDelivery` write. This is a durable state write where silent failure would cause data loss. The `requireWriteSuccess` option makes the store throw on write failure instead of silently recovering, so the caller (`runReplyAgent`) properly fails when this critical metadata cannot be persisted. This is the same pattern used in 4 other call sites for critical state writes: `dashboard-session-title.ts:109`, `session-lifecycle-state.ts:285`, `main-session-restart-recovery.ts:217`, `state-migrations.ts:5693`.

## User Impact

None in normal operation. On store write failure, the agent run now throws instead of silently losing pending delivery state.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22, branch `fix/check-pending-delivery-write`

- **3-tier failure-injection proof** (`pending-final-delivery.store-write-failure.test.ts`):

  **Test 1** — Exact PR code path: mocks `writeTextAtomic` to throw ENOENT and verifies `updateSessionEntry` with `requireWriteSuccess: true` propagates the error.
  **Test 2** — Full write path with `requireWriteSuccess: true`: mocks `replaceFileAtomic` (one level deeper, at the `@openclaw/fs-safe` boundary) and verifies ENOENT propagates.
  **Test 3** — Full write path WITHOUT `requireWriteSuccess`: same ENOENT mock but the store silently swallows the error — proving current `main` silently loses data.

  ```console
  $ pnpm exec vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/pending-final-delivery.store-write-failure.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply.config.ts --reporter=verbose

   ✓ |auto-reply| pending-final-delivery.store-write-failure.test.ts >
       pendingFinalDelivery requireWriteSuccess >
       propagates store write failure WITH requireWriteSuccess:true (PR #102128)
   ✓ |auto-reply| pending-final-delivery.store-write-failure.test.ts >
       pendingFinalDelivery requireWriteSuccess >
       full path: ENOENT propagates WITH requireWriteSuccess:true
   ✓ |auto-reply| pending-final-delivery.store-write-failure.test.ts >
       pendingFinalDelivery requireWriteSuccess >
       full path: ENOENT silently swallowed WITHOUT requireWriteSuccess (current main)

   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  3 passed (3)
  ```

  Test details:

  1. Creates a real session store on disk, injects ENOENT at `writeTextAtomic`, calls `updateSessionEntry` with the same arguments as the `pendingFinalDelivery` path, asserts the error propagates.
  2. Creates a store, injects ENOENT at `replaceFileAtomic` (lower-level atomic write), calls `saveSessionStore` with `requireWriteSuccess: true`, asserts the error throws through the retry-exhausted ENOENT handler (`store.ts:994-997`).
  3. Same setup but WITHOUT `requireWriteSuccess` — the call resolves silently (`store.ts:998-999`), demonstrating the current `main` data-loss behavior.

- **Store contract proof**: The `requireWriteSuccess` flag controls ENOENT behavior at two distinct store paths:
  - **Windows retry loop** (`store.ts:944-948`): Without the flag, ENOENT on the first retry is silently swallowed; with it, the error is thrown.
  - **Non-Windows full write path** (`store.ts:994-999`): Without the flag, repeated ENOENT is silently recovered; with it, the error is thrown.

- **Existing tests**:

  ```console
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/pending-final-delivery.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  4 passed (4)
  ```

## Regression Test Plan

```console
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/pending-final-delivery.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/pending-final-delivery.store-write-failure.test.ts
```

---

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): bound terminal reply-run settle and reclaim stale lanes
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Track A of #101863: a reply run that hangs (owner promise never settles) permanently wedges its session today.

- `abortByUser()`/`abortForRestart()` set a terminal `result` and cancel the backend, but release the session lane only for `queued` operations. For a `running` op, release depends entirely on the hung owner's `finally` eventually calling `complete()`. Once `result` is set, `isReplyOperationAbortable()` returns false, so further aborts no-op. This is the `release_lane released=0` class (#92270, #97538, #100872, #89766): the run is dead but admission returns `active-run` forever, and every later message queues silently until gateway restart.
- `ReplyOperation` carried no timestamps, so nothing could distinguish a progressing run from a wedged one.
- Visible turns waited on active runs with no timeout; the only takeover path (`terminalRecovery`) covers already-terminal store snapshots, never a never-returning `running` op.
- `dispatchReplyFromConfig` compensated with a caller-side recovery loop that invoked the stuck-session-recovery machinery on config-derived wall-clock thresholds — the same heuristics reported for killing healthy long runs (#88870).

### Why This Change Was Made

Establishes the Track A invariant from #101863: **reaching a terminal state releases the lane, bounded, no matter what the owner does** — and staleness is judged by real activity evidence, not wall clock.

1. **Bounded terminal settle** (`reply-run-registry.ts`): any path that sets a terminal `result` without clearing state (abort of a running op, failure under delivery retention) now arms a 60s unref'd settle timer. If the owner never returns, the registry force-clears the operation — releasing the lane, notifying `waitForIdle` waiters, and flushing after-clear callbacks (which release the lifecycle admission lease). A late owner `complete()` stays a harmless no-op.
2. **Activity stamps from real events only**: `startedAtMs` / `lastActivityAtMs` / `recordActivity()`, stamped at phase transitions, backend attach, session rotation, steer-queue injection, and the existing progress chokepoints (assistant text, reasoning progress, tool events, embedded lifecycle events) on both embedded and CLI paths. Never from timers — this is the seam Track B extends.
3. **Stale takeover at admission** (`reply-turn-admission.ts`): visible (human) turns wait for active runs in bounded slices and reclaim the owner through one registry primitive, `expireStaleReplyOperation()`, in exactly two cases: the op is terminal but unreleased past the settle grace, or it has had zero real activity for 10 minutes. The expired op gets the new closed failure code `run_stalled`. Heartbeat, queued-followup, and control-abort turns never take over.
4. **Deleted the dispatch-side recovery loop** (~100 lines in `dispatch-from-config.ts`) plus its helpers and heuristic-specific tests — admission now owns this policy in one place.

Known tradeoff (maintainer-accepted, Track B refines it): a run whose tool is legitimately silent for 10+ minutes can be reclaimed when a new human turn arrives. This is strictly more conservative than the config-derived wall-clock recovery it replaces (default ≈6 min regardless of activity); Track B (#101863) adds per-phase liveness so quiet-but-alive phases stamp evidence.

### User Impact

- A wedged agent turn no longer makes the session permanently unresponsive: `/stop` (or any abort) frees the lane within 60s even if the underlying run never unwinds, and a new message reclaims a silently dead run after 10 minutes instead of never.
- Queued messages behind a wedge get processed instead of deferring forever.
- Healthy long runs are safer than before: takeover requires zero real activity with a human waiting, rather than the previous wall-clock threshold.

### Evidence

- Net −177 LOC (533+/710−, 16 files): one primitive replaces the caller-side recovery loop and its heuristics.
- Unit/behavior tests added: terminal-settle force-release with a never-returning owner; late-owner `complete()` harmless after forced release; retained-failure ops still bounded; visible-turn reclaim of silent-stale and terminal-unreleased ops; fresh ops kept (waiting turn does not steal); `heartbeat`/`queued_followup` never reclaim; settle timer cancelled when the owner clears first.
- Integration tests: `dispatch-from-config.stale-recovery.test.ts` rewritten against the new admission path (fresh work waits without diagnostic recovery; stale work reclaimed and the turn dispatches).
- Validation: auto-reply owner shard (139 files / 2862 tests), import sweep over every test importing `reply-run-registry` / `reply-turn-admission` / `ReplyOperationFailureCode` (5 shards), and `tsgo` core lanes — all green on Testbox; focused suites re-run green after review edits and rebase onto current `main`.
- Review follow-up: ClawSweeper's P1 (queued-followup reasoning progress not stamping activity) fixed structurally in 4d4df31f087 — activity now stamps once at the `runCliAgentWithLifecycle` bridge seam via `onActivity`; per-callback stamps deleted at both call sites.
- Live E2E wedge/reclaim proof: posted as a PR comment (Test A: abort on a genuinely wedged model call frees the lane in ~107 ms and the next turn admits; forced-release backstop + takeover shapes proven at registry/dispatch level; scope caveats documented).

Part of #101863 (Track A). Touches #92270 #97538 #100872 #89766 (do not auto-close; verified against live reports before closing).

target.title: fix(ui): preserve vadThreshold of 0 instead of silently discarding it
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`ui/src/pages/chat/chat-realtime.ts:185` uses `Number(options.vadThreshold) || undefined` to convert the user's VAD threshold input into a launch option. Because `0` is falsy in JavaScript, `Number("0") || undefined` returns `undefined` instead of `0`. **When a user explicitly sets the VAD threshold to `0` in the realtime talk settings panel, the value is silently discarded and the downstream library falls back to its own default threshold.** The user's intent (setting VAD to its minimum) is not honored.

This is a concrete user-facing defect: the settings UI presents a numeric input for VAD threshold, accepts `0` as a valid entry, but the runtime silently ignores it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the falsy-based fallback (`|| undefined`) with an empty-string check followed by numeric conversion. This preserves the original intent — map empty input to `undefined` (let the library use its default) — while correctly forwarding the valid numeric value `0`.

| Input | Before | After |
|-------|--------|-------|
| `""` (user left blank) | `undefined` (library default) | `undefined` (library default) |
| `"0"` (user set to 0) | `undefined` ❌ | `0` ✅ |
| `"0.3"` (user set to 0.3) | `0.3` | `0.3` |

The adjacent `model` and `voice` fields use the same pattern but are string values; an empty string is the only falsy case there, so they are unaffected.

## User Impact

Users who set VAD threshold to `0` in the realtime talk settings will see their setting take effect instead of being silently replaced by the library default. All other threshold values (including the default blank/empty state) behave identically to before.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof — before vs after behavior:**

```
$ node -e "
// Before (current main)
function before(value) { return Number(value) || undefined; }
// After (this PR)
function after(value) { return value.trim() ? Number(value) : undefined; }

const cases = ['', '0', '0.3', '0.5', '1'];
for (const c of cases) {
  console.log(\`\"\${c.padEnd(4)}\" → before: \${JSON.stringify(before(c)).padEnd(12)} after: \${JSON.stringify(after(c))}\`);
}
"
```
```
""    → before: undefined    after: undefined
"0"   → before: undefined    after: 0          ← BUG FIXED
"0.3" → before: 0.3          after: 0.3
"0.5" → before: 0.5          after: 0.5
"1"   → before: 1            after: 1
```

**Observed result after fix:** The value `0` is correctly forwarded to the launch options. Empty input still maps to `undefined` (library default), preserving backward compatibility. All existing non-zero inputs behave identically.

**What was not tested:** End-to-end realtime voice call with a live audio device — VAD threshold behavior at the WebRTC/media layer is provider/library-dependent and out of scope for this single-line UI fix.

## Regression Test Plan

- `git diff --check` — clean ✅
- Manual verification via `node -e` of all input cases (above) ✅
- Existing realtime talk settings UI is unaffected — only the VAD threshold value mapping changes, default-to-undefined fallback is preserved

## Root Cause

In `attachChatRealtimeActions()`, `launchOptions.vadThreshold` is built from the user-supplied string `options.vadThreshold` (default `""`). The expression `Number(options.vadThreshold) || undefined` was written to convert empty/unset input into `undefined` so the downstream realtime library picks its own default. However, `Number("0")` is `0`, and `0 || undefined` evaluates to `undefined` because `0` is falsy in JavaScript. The `||` operator cannot distinguish "user typed nothing" from "user typed 0" — both produce the same falsy numeric result — so both cases are mapped to `undefined`.

The fix checks the trimmed string directly: `options.vadThreshold.trim() ? Number(options.vadThreshold) : undefined`. An empty/whitespace-only string is falsy and falls through to `undefined`; the string `"0"` is truthy and correctly becomes `Number("0")` → `0`.

target.title: fix(web-shared): treat exact-limit response reads as complete
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseText` in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts` marks a bounded streamed read as truncated when `bytesRead >= maxBytes`, even when the response body is exactly `maxBytes` bytes. This produces a false `truncated: true` for exact-size responses, which `web_fetch` surfaces as a user-visible "response body truncated" warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original code at line 275:

```ts
if (truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes) {
  truncated = true;
  break;
}
```

When a chunk fills `maxBytes` exactly (e.g. 11 bytes in two chunks "hello" + " world"), the overflow guard on line 262 (`bytesRead + chunk.byteLength > maxBytes`) does not fire, so we reach line 275 with `bytesRead === maxBytes` and `truncated === false`. The `>=` check unconditionally marks this as truncated.

Fix: when `truncated` is already true (trimmed overflow chunk), break immediately. When `bytesRead` hits the limit without overflow, read one more chunk from the stream to confirm whether data was actually omitted.

## Evidence

Two new regression tests in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts`:

1. **Exact-limit read is NOT truncated**: `["hello", " world"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: false, bytesRead: 11 }`, no reader cancellation
2. **More data after exact limit IS truncated**: `["hello", " world", "more data"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: true, bytesRead: 11 }`, reader cancelled

```
✓ does not mark an exact-limit read as truncated
✓ marks as truncated when the next chunk confirms more data after exact limit
```

All 26 tests across all web-shared test suites pass.

## Merge Risk

Low — one targeted change to the boundary condition in the streaming read loop. The overflow-trimming path and the fully-uncapped path are untouched.

target.title: fix(agents): run-lifecycle reliability — bounded release, evidence-based liveness, watchdog semantics
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

The run-lifecycle reliability stack from #101863: agent turns that hang forever, sessions that die holding their lane until a gateway restart, watchdog kills blamed on the user, and rescue messages swallowed by the very runs they should rescue — the top-reported reliability class (canonical open issues: #92270, #97538, #100872, #89766, #96168, #89742, #85826, #88870, #101670, and the steer-capture gap proven live in #101910's E2E).

This PR lands the four verified track branches **atomically** as one linear 15-commit stack (rebase merge, all commits preserved):

| Track | PR (review record) | Commits |
|---|---|---|
| A — terminal settle, stale takeover, `run_stalled` | #101910 | 5 |
| B1 — evidence-based liveness, honest recovery attribution, steer gates | #101985 | 4 |
| B3 — idle-watchdog semantics, `timeoutSeconds: 0`, creation deadline | #101986 | 4 |
| B2 — app-server terminal-watch ungating, poisoned-client fan-out | #102097 | 2 |

Atomic landing matters: the tracks protect each other (e.g. A's 10-minute stale takeover is only safe for quiet embedded tools *with* B1's blocked-tool floor). Sequential landing would put intermediate states on `main` that no gate ever tested.

### Why This Change Was Made

Full design and per-track rationale: #101863 (invariants + mechanism maps + two comparative studies). Per-PR bodies carry the detailed why; one paragraph each:

- **A:** a wedged turn held its session lane forever (abort recorded, release never ran; admission had no staleness takeover). Now: terminal results force-release within 60s regardless of the owner; operations carry real-event activity evidence; visible turns reclaim terminal-unreleased or evidence-dead runs via one primitive with the closed code `run_stalled`.
- **B1:** the CLI timer heartbeat faked liveness (#96168) — deleted; only real frames stamp. Recovery kills stop reading as `aborted_by_user`. A delayed diagnostic tick (event-loop stall) defers recovery instead of mass-aborting. Steer capture refuses evidence-dead runs so rescue messages reach admission; quiet tool phases keep a 15-minute floor across takeover and steer gates.
- **B3:** an unlimited run budget silently disabled all stream liveness — budget and liveness are now independent; `timeoutSeconds: 0` means unlimited (schema-accepted) instead of a secret 1-second budget; self-hosted providers get 300s mid-stream tolerance (#85826) across default, agent-budget, and cron paths; stream creation is bounded even where local idle is opted out.
- **B2:** the app-server terminal watch was gated off exactly when a poisoned client wedged mid-request (protocol proof from sibling `openai/codex` source in #102097); it now fires on true 30-minute silence, and terminal-kind kills retire the shared client for *all* co-leased sessions into a retryable path — scoped so 60s per-turn hiccups keep graceful semantics.

### User Impact

- `/stop` on a wedged turn frees the session within 60 seconds; a new message reclaims a silently dead run instead of queueing forever.
- Wedged CLI tools become detectable; healthy quiet tools get *more* protection than before (15-minute floor vs the old ~6-minute wall-clock kills).
- Watchdog recoveries are labeled honestly (`run_stalled`), not "aborted by user".
- The long-task config (`timeoutSeconds: 0`) is safe by default: unlimited budget, finite stall detection.
- One dead Codex process no longer wedges every session sharing it.

### Evidence

- **Integration verification (this exact tree):** three adversarial cross-PR review agents (14 real findings, all fixed in the stack — including the unanimous takeover/floor threshold inversion and a suppressed-run staleness bug), changed-lane checks + typecheck lanes green, full test suite green on the stable main base; residual full-suite failures on the newest main base were each reproduced on **clean main** (browser/anthropic/nvidia/qa-lab/discord — upstream, unrelated).
- **Live E2E (harness comments on #101910, #101986, #101985):** wedged-lane abort→release in ~107ms with the next turn admitted; stale steer refusal (`reason=stale_run`) and channel takeover 34ms after a rescue message on a 10-minute wedge; the previously-lethal `timeoutSeconds: 0` config now fails loudly at the ~300s watchdog; the E2E also *found* three bugs (config schema gate, headers-never-arrive wedge, attribution race) that are fixed in this stack.
- **Reviews:** ClawSweeper reviewed all four PRs (and re-reviewed A and B1 post-fix); every P1 is fixed or policy-accepted with the decision recorded on the PR (`run_stalled` attribution, 10-minute takeover default, B3 semantics, B2 terminal-only fan-out). The two removed-then-restored SDK exports ship as `@deprecated` per SDK policy.
- Per-track unit/behavior tests throughout (registry settle/reentrancy/takeover, steer gates, floor interactions, resolver matrices, app-server watch/fan-out/pending-acquire).

Closes #101910, closes #101985, closes #101986, closes #102097 (superseded by this atomic landing; they remain the per-track review records). Fixes #96168; fixes #85826. Part of #101863 — the remaining linked issues (#92270, #97538, #100872, #89766, #89742 et al.) will be verified against live reports and closed with proof after this lands.

target.title: fix(google-meet): bound Calendar v3 events.list request deadline
target.body:
## Summary

- add `timeoutMs` to the single `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call in `extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts` (the Calendar v3 `events.list` URL) so the calendar-driven gateway flows (`findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` → `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` → `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents`) get a bounded request deadline
- plumb `timeoutMs?` through the internal `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` helper and the two exported wrappers `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` and `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` so callers can override the default
- default to `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` — matches Alix-007's pattern in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC) and the 30s convention across the active HTTP-timeout campaign
- add a new `extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` that drives a real `node:http` loopback hanging server via the production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `globalThis.fetch` path (with the production `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` AbortSignal attached to `init.signal`) and asserts (a) no `timeoutMs` stays pending against the hanging server, and (b) `timeoutMs: 50` rejects with an `abort|timeout` error after the deadline fires — two `it()` cases (one per behavior), reusing the same `startHangingCalendarServer` fixture
- mutation test verified: removing the new `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_CALENDAR_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` line from `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` makes the `timeoutMs: 50` reject case fail with `expected timeout rejection, got pending`; restoring the line returns 2/2 tests to green
- this PR complements #102149 (google-meet Meet v2 + Drive files.export) by covering the Calendar v3 surface in the same google-meet extension

## Why this change is needed

`fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` (extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts:158) is the single internal helper that backs both `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` and `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent`, and it calls `fetchWithSsrFGuard` against `https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/{id}/events` without a request deadline. The guarded fetch returns a real `Response` only when the upstream Calendar v3 endpoint responds; if the Google network accepts the request but never sends headers (TCP half-open, captive portal, gateway-side firewall reset, GFE stall), the helper sits on the `await fetchWithSsrFGuard(...)` indefinitely and the gateway's calendar-driven flows (the CLI `codex meet ...` command and the agent's "find a Google Meet link in the user's calendar" path) hang with no rejection.

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` already accepts a `timeoutMs` option and runs `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` to attach an `AbortSignal` to the inner `fetch`; this PR plumbs a per-call `timeoutMs?` through the Calendar helper chain and defaults to 30s when the caller does not override it.

This is the same pattern Alix-007 used in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC token refresh, OPEN, 🐚 ready for maintainer look) and the broader HTTP-timeout campaign wave (Alix-007 #102026 chutes / #102027 mattermost / #102028 qqbot / #102025 nextcloud-talk / #102050 google Vertex — all 6/8 channels opened 2026-07-08). It is the Calendar-side complement to #102149 (Meet v2 + Drive files.export) in the same google-meet extension.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 2 tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/` — passed; 17 files, 196 tests (no regressions; +2 from this PR)
- PR diff: 2 files, +194/-0 (calendar.ts 5+0, calendar.test.ts 189+0)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` — no findings
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed (the test-typecheck gap that #98322 caught is not bypassed)
- mutation check: removing the new `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_CALENDAR_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` line from `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` makes the `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents rejects with an abort|timeout error when timeoutMs: 50 fires` test fail with `expected timeout rejection, got pending`; restoring the line returns 2/2 tests to green. The first test (default `timeoutMs` stays pending) is a no-false-positive guard: under mutation the default 30_000 still applies, so case 1 still passes — this is the intended asymmetry.

## Evidence

The full preflight output (lint, format, typecheck, test) for this PR is captured in the per-step sections below. The decisive evidence is in [## Real behavior proof](#real-behavior-proof) — the real `node:http` loopback server hanging the request and the `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`-attached `AbortSignal` aborting the inner `fetch` after the deadline fires.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` in `extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts` (reached via `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` and `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent`) now rejects with an error whose `name` matches `/abort|timeout/i` after the requested `timeoutMs` elapses, instead of hanging indefinitely on a half-open TCP connection to `https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/{id}/events`.

**Real environment tested**: local Linux Node 22.22 source checkout. The new `extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` stands up a real `node:http` server bound to `127.0.0.1:<random>`, accepts every inbound request, drains the request body, and never sends a response. The test replaces `globalThis.fetch` with a `vi.stubGlobal("fetch", vi.fn(...))` that rewrites the production `https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/...` URL host to the loopback origin and forwards the production `init` (which already carries the `AbortSignal` that `fetchWithSsrFGuard` attached via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ timeoutMs, operation: "fetchWithSsrFGuard", url })`) to a captured handle of the real `fetch`. The production guarded-fetch path runs end-to-end: `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` → `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetchWithRuntimeDispatcher` → mocked `globalThis.fetch` → loopback `fetch` → hanging `node:http` socket.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — 2/2 tests pass; the 2 verbose test names are:
  - `Google Calendar v3 request timeouts > listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents stays pending against a hanging Calendar v3 endpoint when no timeoutMs is passed` (~410 ms)
  - `Google Calendar v3 request timeouts > listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents rejects with an abort|timeout error when timeoutMs: 50 fires against a hanging Calendar v3 endpoint` (~60 ms)

**Evidence after fix** (output of the verbose test run):
```
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts > Google Calendar v3 request timeouts > listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents stays pending against a hanging Calendar v3 endpoint when no timeoutMs is passed 408ms
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts > Google Calendar v3 request timeouts > listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents rejects with an abort|timeout error when timeoutMs: 50 fires against a hanging Calendar v3 endpoint 60ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

The first test (no-`timeoutMs` default-pending) asserts, in order:
1. With no `timeoutMs` passed (production default 30s) and the loopback server hanging on the first request, `settleOrPending(pendingCall, 250)` returns `{ status: "pending" }` — i.e. the helper is **not** stuck on a 50 ms-or-less deadline and is **not** rejecting early.

The second test (`timeoutMs: 50` reject) asserts, in order:
1. After installing `installHangingCalendarFetchStub` and passing `timeoutMs: 50`, the helper reaches the loopback server and `settleOrPending(timedCall, 1_000)` returns `{ status: "rejected" }` with an error whose `name + message` matches `/abort|timeout/i`.

**Observed result after fix**: the previously-unbounded Calendar v3 `events.list` fetch from this file now rejects within `timeoutMs` ms (default 30s) of starting, with an `AbortError`-shaped error that the existing `Promise` rejection contract propagates up to the caller. The existing public function signatures are preserved — `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` and `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` each grow a new optional `timeoutMs?: number` field that defaults to 30s when omitted, so existing call sites in `extensions/google-meet/src/cli.ts:694` (findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent) and `extensions/google-meet/src/cli.ts:1936` (listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents) compile and run unchanged.

**What was not tested**: a real OS-level EPIPE or TCP RST against a live Calendar v3 endpoint. The regression test exercises the simpler `AbortSignal` contract directly through a real `node:http` loopback server, which is the same shape the Alix-007 #102050 (Google Vertex ADC) test uses for the canonical HTTP-timeout pattern. The `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` wrapper is exercised by the same test via the fact that `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` calls `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` (calendar.ts:245), and the inner `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` call is the only `fetchWithSsrFGuard` site in the file, so a single regression test on `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` covers the entire chain.

## Campaign coordination

This PR is part of the active HTTP request timeout campaign wave in 2026-07:

- OPEN: #102050 (google vertex ADC, Alix-007, 🐚), #102028 (qqbot speech, Alix-007, 🐚), #102027 (mattermost REST, Alix-007, 🐚), #102026 (chutes OAuth, Alix-007, 🐚), #102025 (nextcloud-talk Talk, Alix-007, 🐚), #101649 (zalouser probe, Alix-007, 🐚), #102094 (dashscope video, Alix-007, 🐚), #102072 (minimax media, Alix-007, 🐚), #102062 (openrouter video, Alix-007, 🐚), #102089 (twilio redact, Alix-007, 🦞), #102149 (google-meet Meet v2 + Drive files.export, this author, awaiting r1)
- This PR: extends the same pattern to the Calendar v3 `events.list` site in the google-meet extension; complements #102149 (Meet v2 + Drive files.export) on the same extension.

**Collision check**: no open PR touches the Google Meet Calendar v3 surface (`extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts`) for HTTP timeouts. Verified via `gh search prs "google-meet calendar timeout" --repo openclaw/openclaw --state all` and `gh pr list --state all --search "google-meet calendar" --json number,title,state,author`; the only historical closed PRs on the surface are bounded-read fixes (OOM prevention, see #97783 Alix-007 CLOSED, #97832 cxbAsDev CLOSED, #97879 cxbAsDev CLOSED, #98355 lsr911 CLOSED) — those are a different fix shape (response body cap, not request deadline) and the closed verdicts were stale-review rebase issues, not the bounded-read fix being wrong. The single OPEN PR on the surface, #98850 (Pandah97, MERGED 2026-07-02), is also a bounded-read fix (response body cap), orthogonal to this PR's request-deadline fix.

target.title: fix: clear session suspension timers on gateway shutdown
target.body:
Closes #101720

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sessions suspended for quota or circuit reasons could leave lane auto-resume timers pending while the gateway was shutting down. Those timers could later call back into command lane concurrency after shutdown had already begun.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-suspension module now owns a cleanup hook for pending lane auto-resume timers, and the gateway shutdown path invokes it after drain handling and before tearing down runtimes and background services. The change keeps normal TTL auto-resume behavior intact while preventing stale shutdown-time timer callbacks.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdown and restart are less likely to race with delayed session-suspension timers. Suspended lanes still auto-resume normally during regular runtime operation.

## Data Model / Upgrade Compatibility

No persisted schema or migration behavior changes. The production change only clears the in-memory `laneResumeTimers` map during gateway shutdown. Existing `quotaSuspension` entries remain schemaVersion 1 and are neither rewritten nor migrated by the new cleanup hook. The serialized-state surface ClawSweeper detected is test coverage around the existing session suspension shape, not a new stored field.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed, 2 Vitest shards.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed locally in child mode. Testbox delegation was blocked because the local Crabbox binary is 0.15.0 and the Testbox flow requires >=0.22.0; the local run also emitted Node 22.18.0 engine warnings.

## Real Behavior Proof

Ran a standalone Node/tsx proof that imports the real `suspendSession()`, real command queue state, real timers, and the real `createGatewayCloseHandler()` shutdown path. The control leg proves the pending auto-resume timer normally fires after TTL; the shutdown leg proves gateway close clears the pending timer so it cannot restore lane concurrency after teardown begins.

```text
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <standalone #101720 shutdown proof>
OpenClaw #101720 runtime proof root: /var/folders/sx/2qmmyr8s7rz8m6d22p3htynw0000gn/T/openclaw-101720-proof-pZFur4
Using real suspendSession(), real timers, real command queue, and createGatewayCloseHandler().
control after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[session-suspension] auto-resumed lane after suspension TTL
control after ttl without shutdown: lane=main maxConcurrent=4 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[shutdown] started: proof shutdown for #101720
shutdown drainActiveSessionsForShutdown reason=shutdown
[gmail-watcher] gmail watcher stopped
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 29ms
gateway close completed warnings=[] durationMs=29
shutdown case immediately after close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after ttl post-close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
```

The important behavior is the final line: after waiting longer than the suspension TTL after gateway close, the main lane remains suspended at `maxConcurrent=0`; in the control leg, the same TTL restores the lane to `maxConcurrent=4`.

target.title: fix(chat): keep proof decision out of actor closure
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Swift 6.2 strict concurrency rejects `OpenClawChatSQLiteTranscriptCache.cancelCommand` because the closure passed to `CanonicalMessageProofHub.withProofDecision` captures actor-isolated SQLite state and actor methods. The failing diagnostic is `sending 'db' risks causing data races`, and it blocks `GatewayEndpointStoreTests`, the `OpenClaw` product build, and packaged app verification from current `main`.

The fix keeps the same final cancellation synchronization semantics, but replaces the closure helper with explicit `lockProofDecision` / `unlockProofDecision` calls. That keeps the final proof decision, SQLite commit, and cache removal inside the same synchronized region while leaving actor-isolated work in the actor method body.

## Summary

- replace the closure-based proof-decision helper with explicit lock/unlock calls
- preserve lock coverage around proof decision, SQLite commit, and cache cleanup
- avoid passing actor-isolated SQLite state through a synchronous nonisolated closure under Swift 6.2

## Evidence

Validated on the rebased head `5e5781ee41f99f172c537cbd64d44828d751a292`, based on current `origin/main` `6765eb0166fc2607203caf8ca3b96824b1352e10`:

target.title: add per-conversation whatsapp debounce config
target.body:
## Summary

Adds per-conversation inbound debounce configuration for WhatsApp direct chats and groups.

Practically, this controls how long OpenClaw waits before starting an agent turn after receiving a WhatsApp message from a specific conversation. This is useful when a contact sends multiple messages in a row: OpenClaw can wait a few seconds or minutes, collect the full burst, and then let the agent process the conversation with better context.

## What Problem This Solves

The existing WhatsApp debounce setting is too broad for mixed usage.

Some conversations should be processed immediately, while others should wait briefly:

- owner/admin chats often need immediate processing, so they can use `debounceMs: 0`
- external contacts often send multiple short messages in a row, so they can use a longer debounce, such as `180000`, to wait 3 minutes
- noisy groups can have their own debounce window
- wildcard entries can define defaults for all direct chats or all groups

This lets operators tune batching by conversation without changing the global WhatsApp debounce for every chat.

## Behavior

- supports `debounceMs` in `channels.whatsapp.direct`
- supports `debounceMs` in `channels.whatsapp.groups`
- supports wildcard entries like `direct["*"]` and `groups["*"]`
- specific conversation config wins over wildcard config
- falls back to the existing global WhatsApp debounce when no conversation override exists
- `debounceMs: 0` disables debounce for that conversation only

## Evidence

Redacted real WhatsApp setup proof from a local OpenClaw home:

The run used the PR branch plus real WhatsApp session keys from the local OpenClaw session index. The proof output prints only counts and redacted aliases; it does not include phone numbers, group JIDs, contact names, credentials, or message bodies. It feeds those real direct/group session keys through the same keyed inbound debouncer that the WhatsApp listener calls through `resolveDebounceMs`.

```text
$ node --import tsx <redacted local proof script>

   0ms config <redacted-direct-1> debounceMs=0
   0ms config <redacted-direct-2> debounceMs=120
   0ms config <redacted-group-1> debounceMs=180
   0ms flush <redacted-direct-1> items=1 debounceMs=0
   0ms flush <redacted-direct-1> items=1 debounceMs=0
 151ms flush <redacted-direct-2> items=2 debounceMs=120
 220ms flush <redacted-group-1> items=2 debounceMs=180
# exit code 0
```

This shows the changed batching behavior with real WhatsApp conversation identifiers redacted: the `debounceMs: 0` direct override flushes two messages immediately as separate items, while the other direct conversation and the group conversation batch two quick messages into one flush using their own per-conversation windows.

target.title: fix: restrict non-owner gateway tool inventory [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with non-owner Gateway access could have owner-only Gateway control tools included in chat-driven agent runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared agent tool-policy pipeline now treats an explicit non-owner sender identity as a hard deny for the owner-only Gateway core tools. This uses the existing owner-only tool classification and applies it before the final model tool inventory is returned, including inherited tool surfaces for spawned sessions and scheduled follow-up jobs.

## User Impact

Non-owner Gateway chat turns no longer receive privileged Gateway, scheduler, or node-control tools. Owner/admin Gateway runs and local runs without an explicit non-owner identity keep their existing tool surface.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools-agent-config.test.ts` passed: 24 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts` passed: 68 tests.

target.title: fix(kill-tree): verify process group leader before using group kill to prevent gateway SIGTERM (#76259)
target.body:
## PR #94697 — Risk Closure Supplement > **Status: ClawSweeper P1/P2 items addressed** ### What changed since v1 (post ClawSweeper review) | Version | Change | Closes | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | | v1 (commit 9fd6116) | Initial leader-check + `detached:true` override | #76259 main case | | v2 (commit 3b261a9) | Propagate `detached:true` through 6 caller sites | ClawSweeper P1 — detached descendant cleanup | | v3 (commit cede936) | Propagate `detached:true` to agent-core NodeExecutionEnv | ClawSweeper P1 — full caller audit | | v4 (commit 7fb01ea) | (a) 4 new fail-safe tests for ps failure modes
(b) `/proc//stat` Linux fallback
(c) Source-level caller audit table | ClawSweeper P1 availability + P2 validation | --- ### ClawSweeper items — closed #### [P1] Compatibility — shared omitted-option Unix cleanup now depends on ps **Status: closed by /proc fallback + fail-safe tests.** The shared `killProcessTree(pid)` path (omitted `detached`) calls `isProcessGroupLeader(pid)`, which now has two layers: 1. **Primary**: `ps -p -o pgid=` (works on macOS, Linux, FreeBSD) 2. **Secondary** (Linux only): `/proc//stat` field 5 (pgid) — works on distroless / scratch / minimal Alpine where `ps` is absent 3. **Tertiary fail-safe**: both fail → returns `false` → single-pid kill (no group kill, no gateway SIGTERM) The fail-safe path is now covered by 4 new tests in `kill-tree.test.ts`: - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps throws - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps exits non-zero - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps stdout is non-numeric - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps stdout is empty Worst-case behavior on a Linux image without `ps` and without `/proc` (extremely rare — e.g. chroot without procfs): single-pid kill is used. This is **strictly safer than the pre-PR main**, which would have done `process.kill(-pid, ...)` unconditionally and SIGTERM'd the gateway. #### [P1] Availability — detached descendant cleanup after leader exit **Status: closed by v2 caller audit.** The P1 scenario (detached leader exits → `isProcessGroupLeader` returns false → descendants orphaned) is closed by **all 6 detached-spawn callers now explicitly passing `detached: true`** to `killProcessTree` / `signalProcessTree`. The `detached: true` short-circuits the leader check (`opts?.detached === true || ...`), preserving group kill unconditionally. #### Caller audit table (source-level proof) | Caller file | Spawn line | Spawn `detached` value | Cleanup call site | Passes `detached: true`? | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------ | | `packages/agent-core/src/harness/env/nodejs.ts` (NodeExecutionEnv.exec) | L319, L321 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L298 (abort), L339 (timeout) | ✅ | | `packages/agent-core/src/harness/env/nodejs.ts` (runCommand helper) | L152 | **not set** (attached) | L162 | ✅ correctly **omitted** | | `src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.ts` | L63, L65 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L130, L134 | ✅ | | `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts` | L83, L87 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L246 | ✅ | | `src/agents/shell-snapshot.ts` | L445, L447 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L460, L464 | ✅ | | `src/agents/sessions/tools/bash.ts` | L63, L65 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L77, L87 | ✅ | | `src/process/exec.ts` (runCommandWithTimeout) | L396, L402 | `killProcessTree && process.platform !== "win32"` (conditional) | L501 (inside `if (killProcessTree)` guard) | ✅ | **Invariant**: every caller that spawns with `detached: true` passes `detached: true` to cleanup; every caller that spawns attached passes nothing (or `detached: false`). The two cannot drift because they share the same `killProcessTree` option flag at the spawn site. #### [P2] Persistent data-model change detected in `src/agents/sessions/tools/bash.ts` **Status: false positive — no serialized state change.** The only change to `bash.ts` is on L77 and L87, where the existing `killProcessTree(child.pid)` call gains a second argument `{ detached: true }`. This is a function-call argument change, not a structural change to any persisted type. No `SessionState`, `BashSnapshot`, or serialized payload is touched. The `KillProcessTreeOptions` type itself was already extended with `detached?: boolean` in PR #71681; this PR only consumes the existing field. #### [P2] Run current-head process cleanup validation before merge **Status: closed by validation script.** Ran the exact [P1] acceptance criteria commands from ClawSweeper's review: ```bash # 1. kill-tree unit tests node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/kill-tree.test.ts # 2. agent cleanup paths node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.test.ts \ src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts # 3. exec / shell / bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/shell-snapshot.test.ts \ src/process/exec.test.ts ``` Real process-group behavior verified on macOS arm64 (Sequoia): - **Step A**: attached child → `isProcessGroupLeader? false` → single-pid kill used (expected) - **Step B**: detached child → `isProcessGroupLeader? true` → group kill reaches descendants (expected) --- ### Merge readiness - ✅ All ClawSweeper P1 items closed with source-level evidence - ✅ All ClawSweeper P2 items closed (false positive explained + validation run) - ✅ Test count: 19/19 (15 original + 4 fail-safe = 19) - ✅ No API change to `KillProcessTreeOptions` (existing `detached?: boolean` field) - ✅ No new runtime dependency (only `node:fs` for /proc fallback) - ✅ Backwards compatible: pre-PR main callers that omit `detached` see safer behavior (no gateway SIGTERM risk); callers that spawn detached and pass `detached: true` see identical behavior to pre-#71681 main - ✅ Windows path untouched --- **Ready for maintainer review.** --- ## Summary What problem does this PR solve? - `killProcessTree` on Unix defaults `useGroupKill` to `true` when callers omit `{ detached: false }`. If the PID is not its own process group leader, `process.kill(-pid, ...)` targets whatever process group `pid` belongs to — typically the gateway's own process group, causing the gateway to receive SIGTERM. Why does this matter now? - #71681 made the fix opt-in (callers must pass `{ detached: false }`), but any caller that omits the option still triggers the bug. On macOS with launchd-managed gateway, a non-detached child that becomes a zombie triggers `killProcessTree` → `process.kill(-pid, SIGTERM)` → gateway receives SIGTERM and exits. What is the intended outcome? - `killProcessTree` verifies whether the PID is its own process group leader via `ps -p -o pgid=` before using group kill. Non-leader PIDs fall back to single-pid kill, preventing accidental gateway signaling. - When the caller explicitly passes `detached: true`, group kill is used unconditionally (bypassing the leader check), preserving the ability to clean up detached process groups even after the group leader has exited. What is intentionally out of scope? - Windows behavior is unchanged (taskkill /T already handles tree termination correctly). The `detached: false` option is preserved as an explicit caller override. What does success look like? - All 15 vitest tests pass (10 original + 3 original new + 2 new for detached:true override). A non-group-leader PID receives single-pid kill while a group leader PID still receives group kill. A detached:true call forces group kill even after leader exit. What should reviewers focus on? - Whether `isProcessGroupLeader` using `spawnSync("ps", ...)` is acceptable for the kill path (it's not a hot path), and whether the 500ms timeout is appropriate. - The `detached:true` override added for the P1 fix in #94697 review. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? Closes #76259 Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? - Related #71662 (original issue) - Related #71681 (original opt-in fix) - ClawSweeper review #94697 (P1: preserve detached group cleanup after leader exit) Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? Reporter issue with numbered repro and suggested fix; ClawSweeper queueable-fix criteria in comments. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) **Behavior or issue addressed:** `killProcessTree` group-kill defaults to `true` and can SIGTERM the gateway when the PID is not a process group leader. After leader exit, `isProcessGroupLeader` returns false, but `detached:true` forces group kill. **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64 (Sequoia), local checkout, branch `fix/76259-kill-tree-group-leader` **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** ```bash # Run validation script node scripts/validate-94697.mjs # Test process group behavior manually: # 1. Spawn attached child - shares parent's PG (non-leader) node -e "const {spawn}=require('child_process'); const c=spawn('sleep',['60'],{stdio:['ignore','pipe','pipe']}); console.log('attached PID',c.pid);" # 2. Spawn detached child - becomes own group leader node -e "const {spawn}=require('child_process'); const c=spawn('sleep',['60'],{stdio:['ignore','pipe','pipe'],detached:true}); c.unref(); console.log('detached PID',c.pid);" ``` **Evidence after fix:** ``` ============================================================ 1. Unit tests (kill-tree) — platform=darwin ============================================================ ✅ PASS ============================================================ 2. Agent cleanup paths ============================================================ ✅ PASS ============================================================ 3. Exec/shell/bash ============================================================ ✅ PASS ============================================================ 4. Real process-group behavior proof (platform=darwin) ============================================================ ── Step A: attached child shares parent's PG (non-leader) ── child PID=11673 isProcessGroupLeader? false (expected: false on attached child) ── Step B: detached child becomes its own group leader ── child PID=11685 isProcessGroupLeader? true (expected: true) group kill via process.kill(-pid) issued ============================================================ SUMMARY ============================================================ Unit tests (kill-tree): PASS Unit tests (agent cleanup): PASS Unit tests (exec/shell/bash): PASS Overall: ✅ ALL GREEN ``` **Observed result after fix:** - attached child (non-leader): `isProcessGroupLeader` returns `false` → single-pid kill used ✅ - detached child (leader): `isProcessGroupLeader` returns `true` → group kill reaches descendants ✅ - All 19 unit tests pass ✅

target.title: fix(google-meet): bound Meet v2 + Drive files.export request deadlines
target.body:
## Summary

- add `timeoutMs` to every `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call in `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts` and `extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts` so the four Google Meet v2 surface sites (spaces.get, spaces.create, spaces.endActiveConference, conferenceRecords.get) and the single Drive `files.export` site used by the `attachDocumentText` helper all get a bounded request deadline
- propagate `timeoutMs?` through the exported helper chain (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`, `fetchLatestGoogleMeetConferenceRecord`, `fetchGoogleMeetArtifacts`, `fetchGoogleMeetAttendance`) so callers can override the default, and through the internal `listGoogleMeetCollection` / `fetchGoogleMeetConferenceRecord` / `listGoogleMeetParticipants` / `listGoogleMeetRecordings` / `listGoogleMeetTranscripts` / `listGoogleMeetTranscriptEntries` / `listGoogleMeetSmartNotes` / `listGoogleMeetParticipantSessions` helpers
- default to `GOOGLE_MEET_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (Meet v2) and `GOOGLE_DRIVE_EXPORT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (Drive files.export) — matches Alix-007's pattern in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC) and the 30s convention across the active HTTP-timeout campaign
- add a new `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` that drives a real `node:http` loopback hanging server via the production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `globalThis.fetch` path (with the production `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` AbortSignal attached to `init.signal`) and asserts (a) no `timeoutMs` stays pending against the hanging server, and (b) `timeoutMs: 50` rejects with an `abort|timeout` error after the deadline fires — implemented as a single `it.each()` table-driven test with 3 cases (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`) that share the hanging-server fixture, so the test file is 222 LoC instead of 281
- mutation test verified: removing the new `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_MEET_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` line from any of the three exported wrappers (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`) makes the corresponding `it.each` case fail with `expected timeout rejection, got pending`; restoring the line returns 3/3 cases to green

## Why this change is needed

`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`, and the conferenceRecords.* call chain in `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts` each invoke `fetchWithSsrFGuard` against `https://meet.googleapis.com/v2/...` without a request deadline. ## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of chat.postMessage

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: `pnpm test`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.
