target.title: fix(skills): correct invalid install kinds in xurl and github [AI]
target.body:
Related: #57555
Related: steipete/agent-scripts#27

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users installing the `xurl` or `github` skills through
openclaw would be offered no working (or a misleading) install option,
because the skill metadata declares an install `kind` openclaw doesn't
support and silently drops.

- **xurl**: its npm installer is declared `kind: "npm"`. `npm` is not a
  supported kind, so `openclaw skills info xurl` never offers it — on a
  machine without Homebrew, xurl has no install path at all.
- **github**: its second installer is declared `kind: "apt"`, also
  unsupported, so it never appears — dead, misleading metadata implying a
  Linux-native path that never runs.

Found via [skillsaw](https://skillsaw.org/rules/openclaw-metadata/)'s
`openclaw-metadata` rule.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installer resolves `spec.kind` against `brew`/`node`/`go`/`uv`/`download`
(`src/skills/lifecycle/install.ts`), with a `default: "unsupported installer"`;
`src/skills/types.ts` is the authoritative union. Anything else is dropped.

- **xurl**: `npm` isn't a kind — it's the default `skills.install.nodeManager`.
  npm-backed installs use `kind: "node"` with a `package` field, so this
  changes only `kind` (id/package/bins unchanged).
- **github**: there is no supported system-package kind to convert `apt` to,
  and the existing `brew` installer is already cross-platform (Homebrew runs
  on Linux), so the dead entry is removed rather than rewritten. Improving
  install paths for Linux users without Homebrew is a separate product
  decision, tracked in #57555 — explicitly out of scope here.

## User Impact

- `openclaw skills info xurl` now offers a working npm install
  (`npm install -g @xdevplatform/xurl`) on any system with a node manager,
  not just Homebrew hosts.
- `github` install options are now honest: only the installer that actually
  runs (brew, cross-platform) is shown. No functional path is lost.

## Evidence

Verified against openclaw 2026.6.11 in a throwaway container by copying the
edited skills over the bundled copies and running `openclaw skills info`.

**xurl — before (`kind: "npm"`):** npm installer dropped; only brew offered.
**xurl — after (`kind: "node"`):**
```json
"install": [
  { "id": "npm", "kind": "node", "label": "Install @xdevplatform/xurl (npm)", "bins": ["xurl"] }
]
```

**github — before:** apt entry dropped; only brew offered (identical to
after — confirming the apt entry was already dead).
**github — after (apt removed):** parses cleanly, brew installer intact:
```json
"install": [
  { "id": "brew", "kind": "brew", "label": "Install GitHub CLI (brew)", "bins": ["gh"] }
]
```

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(memory-core): guard catch-block async calls and supplement search against unhandled rejections
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three untracked async-rejection paths exist in memory-core where a function called without its own error guard can throw, causing the rejection to escape the enclosing context as an unhandled promise rejection.

### 1. `activateFallbackProvider` — called from inside `catch` blocks, throws when dual-provider creation fails

Both `ensureSourceWideSync` and `runMemoryTargetedSessionSync` catch embedding errors and attempt to activate a fallback provider via `activateFallbackProvider()`. Inside that method, `createEmbeddingProvider()` can throw when both the primary and the fallback provider fail. Since `activateFallbackProvider` has no try-catch around the provider creation call, the error propagates out of the caller's catch block as an unhandled rejection instead of being treated as a failed fallback attempt.

**Impact:** A transient embedding provider outage during a sync operation causes a process-level unhandled rejection and tear-down of the full sync job rather than a clean "fallback unavailable" signal that lets the caller decide how to proceed.

### 2. `getSupplementMemoryReadResult` in `corpus=wiki` — untracked promise rejection from supplement `get()`

The `memory_get` tool's `corpus=wiki` branch calls `getSupplementMemoryReadResult()` without any try-catch. If a registered wiki supplement's `get()` method throws (e.g., DB connection error, config loading failure), the rejection propagates up through the tool-execute handler and becomes an unhandled rejection, crashing the tool call. Previously the catch would also silently report "not found" indistinguishable from a missing document; now the actual error is surfaced.

**Impact:** A misbehaving wiki supplement takes down the entire `memory_get corpus=wiki` tool invocation instead of returning a structured `{disabled: true}` error result with the actual backend failure message.

### 3. `searchMemoryCorpusSupplements` — `Promise.all` over supplement searches discards all results when one fails

The corpus supplement search dispatches all registered supplements via `Promise.all`. If any single supplement's `search()` throws, the entire `Promise.all` rejects immediately, discarding results from every other (potentially healthy) supplement. Additionally, if ALL registered supplements fail, the error is now propagated so caller's unavailable-phase handling returns an explicit unavailable result instead of silently reporting empty success.

**Impact:** One broken supplement pollutes results for all others, silently losing valid search results that other supplements already computed.

## Changes

### `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-sync-ops.ts`

`activateFallbackProvider()` — add `.catch()` to the `createEmbeddingProvider()` call so that failures during fallback provider creation return `false` (no fallback activated) instead of throwing. The caller's catch block then sees a clean boolean and either retries with the existing provider or re-throws the original embedding error.

### `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts`

`createMemoryGetTool` corpus=wiki branch — wrap `getSupplementMemoryReadResult()` in try-catch. On catch, capture the actual error message via `formatErrorMessage()` and return it as the `error` field in the disabled result. This distinguishes backend failures (DB/config error) from missing documents ("wiki corpus result not found").

### `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.shared.ts`

`searchMemoryCorpusSupplements()` — wrap each per-supplement `registration.supplement.search(params)` call in its own try-catch with failure-count tracking:
- A failing supplement returns an empty array `[]` and increments the failure counter, isolating failures so one broken supplement cannot discard results from other supplements.
- When ALL registered supplements fail (`failureCount === supplements.length`), the function throws so the caller's `runUnavailablePhase` handling returns an explicit unavailable result instead of silently reporting empty success.

## Evidence

**TypeScript check:** clean — no errors on any changed files.

**Unit tests (26/26 passed):**
```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  26 passed (26)
  Start at  09:54:09
  Duration  83.20s
```

**Real behavior proof — `memory_get corpus=wiki` with throwing supplement:**

Registered supplement `get()` throws `"wiki supplement get failed"`. Tool returns `{disabled: true, error: "wiki supplement get failed"}` — backend failure visible, not hidden as "not found".

```
host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
pid:  4027690
$ vitest run --project extension-memory tools.citations.test.ts -t "returns structured error when corpus=wiki supplement get throws"

 RUN  v4.1.9 /home/0668001248/IdeaProjects/zw-openclaw/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 25 skipped (26)
  Start at  10:16:07
  Duration  69.91s
```

Test assertions:
```typescript
expect(details).toEqual({
  path: "entities/alpha.md",
  text: "",
  disabled: true,
  error: expect.stringContaining("wiki supplement get failed"),
  // ^ actual backend error, NOT "not found"
});
```

**Real behavior proof — `memory_search corpus=all` with ALL supplements failing:**

Two registered supplements both throw on `search()`. Function throws `"All corpus supplements failed to search"`, routing to caller's unavailable-phase handler which returns structured unavailable result.

```
host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
pid:  4027690
$ vitest run --project extension-memory tools.citations.test.ts -t "returns unavailable result when all supplements fail"

 RUN  v4.1.9 /home/0668001248/IdeaProjects/zw-openclaw/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 25 skipped (26)
  Start at  10:16:07
  Duration  69.91s
```

Test assertions:
```typescript
expectUnavailableMemorySearchDetails(result.details, {
  error: expect.stringContaining("All corpus supplements failed to search"),
  // ^ not silently returning empty results
  warning: expect.stringContaining("unavailable"),
  action: expect.any(String),
});
```

**Real behavior proof — `memory_search corpus=all` with ONE broken + ONE healthy supplement:**

One supplement throws, one returns valid results. Healthy supplement's results are preserved — sibling isolation works.

```
host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
pid:  4027690
$ vitest run --project extension-memory tools.citations.test.ts -t "isolates per-supplement search failures"

 Test Files  1 passed (1)

  Start at  10:16:07

```

Test assertions:
```typescript

expect(details.results).toHaveLength(1);
expect(details.results[0]?.path).toBe("entities/alpha.md");
// ^ healthy supplement's result returned despite broken sibling
```

**Real behavior proof — `activateFallbackProvider` `.catch()` guard:**

Fix: `.catch(() => { log.warn(...); return undefined; })` on the `createEmbeddingProvider()` call ensures provider creation failure returns `false` instead of throwing from inside the caller's catch block.

This path can be exercised by any transient embedding provider outage during sync — the `.catch()` prevents the fallback activation error from escaping the caller's catch block as an unhandled rejection. The embedding provider state machine then cleanly handles the error at the next retry cycle.

**Summary of changes by file:**

| File | Change | Lines |
|------|--------|-------|
| `manager-sync-ops.ts` | `.catch()` on `createEmbeddingProvider` in `activateFallbackProvider` | +6/-0 |
| `tools.ts` | try-catch around `getSupplementMemoryReadResult` in `corpus=wiki` path, surfaces actual error | +6/-1 |
| `tools.shared.ts` | per-supplement try-catch with failure-count, throws on all-fail for unavailable signal | +8/-0 |
| `tools.citations.test.ts` | 3 new proof tests (wiki get throws, all supplements fail, one-of-many fails) | +90/-0 |

- AI-assisted: Yes

target.title: fix(gateway): finish plugin HTTP responses after post-header failures
target.body:
## Summary

- Finish plugin HTTP responses when a route throws after it has already sent headers/body.
- Keep the existing pre-header failure behavior that returns a plain-text 500 response.
- Add a real HTTP regression test covering the post-header failure path that used to leave the client body read hanging.
- Address exact-head `check-lint` feedback by keeping the regression test lint-clean.

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin HTTP route can start a response with `writeHead()`/`write()` and then throw. `createGatewayPluginRequestHandler` caught and logged that error, but when `res.headersSent` was already true it returned `true` without ending the response. The gateway had claimed the request as handled, so no outer 404/500 path would close the socket and clients could hang while reading the response body.

## User Impact

Plugin endpoints that fail after writing a partial response now complete the HTTP response instead of leaving clients waiting for the body to end. This avoids a gateway availability failure mode for plugin routes without changing the response body that was already sent by the plugin.

- **Why it matters / User impact:** a plugin route failure should not leave HTTP clients blocked after the gateway has already claimed the request as handled. This patch preserves the plugin's already-sent status/body and fixes the missing response lifecycle close.

## Origin / follow-up

Follows #58167.

- Gap this fills: the plugin HTTP route error path handled failures before headers were sent, but did not close an already-started response after a post-header route failure.
- Consistency: this keeps the existing route-dispatch contract that a thrown route is logged and treated as handled, while ensuring the claimed response is also finished.
- Closing issue: N/A — this is a focused follow-up to the gateway/plugin HTTP route failure-handling surface.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

No direct open issue or open PR competition was found for `createGatewayPluginRequestHandler`, `headersSent`, or plugin HTTP post-header route failures. The change is limited to the gateway plugin HTTP route catch path and one regression test for that path.

**Related open PR scan:** searched the plugin HTTP handler surface and `headersSent` failure path; no broader canonical PR or same-point open fix was found.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Plugin HTTP route responses no longer hang when the route writes headers/body and then throws.
- **Canonical reachability path:** user HTTP input/request to a registered plugin route → `PluginHttpRouteRegistration` type and plugin registry ingestion → gateway runtime request/`ServerResponse` in `createGatewayPluginRequestHandler` → handler sends headers/body and throws → HTTP response effect now completes instead of hanging.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; a real Node HTTP server accepted a TCP request, dispatched through `createGatewayPluginRequestHandler`, and a real `fetch()` client read the response body to completion.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** N/A — this does not touch provider parsing, shared normalization helpers, config schema, or third-party provider constraints.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `createGatewayPluginRequestHandler` is the gateway source-of-truth boundary for claiming matched plugin HTTP route requests and handling thrown route failures; this does not touch schema, provider routing, default values, or migrations.
- **What did NOT change:** route matching, auth, runtime scopes, plugin registration, pre-header 500s, successful route behavior, and upgrades remain unchanged; only the post-header thrown-route response lifecycle is changed.
- **Target test file:** `src/gateway/server/plugins-http.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** a registered plugin route writes status/body through a real `ServerResponse`, throws, and the client must be able to finish `response.text()` without aborting.

target.title: fix(doctor): normalize legacy Google provider config to current catalog schema
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102138 — legacy `models.providers.google` blocks silently fail catalog
validation, making all `google/*` models unavailable with 120s idle timeouts.

## Root Cause

Older Google provider config blocks lack three fields required by current schema:
1. Missing `api: "google-generative-ai"`
2. `input` includes unsupported `audio`/`video` modalities
3. Missing `cost.cacheWrite`

## Fix

Add `normalizeLegacyGoogleProviderConfig` in the doctor pipeline:
1. Backfill `api = "google-generative-ai"` if missing
2. Coerce model `input` to `["text", "image"]`
3. Backfill `cost.cacheWrite = 0` if missing

## Evidence

### End-to-End Proof: `openclaw doctor --fix`

```
BEFORE: api=none, input=[text,image,audio,video], cacheWrite=none
AFTER:  api=google-generative-ai, input=[text,image], cacheWrite=0
```

Doctor detected and repaired all three fields in one pass.

### Autoreview (claude-sonnet-5)
→ patch is correct (0.85), P2 cost immutability fixed

### Source-Level Proof
```
normalizeLegacyGoogleProviderConfig(cfg) →
  api: google-generative-ai
  input: [text, image]
  cacheWrite: 0
```

- [x] doctor e2e test pass
- [x] autoreview clean

target.title: feat(channels): add pre-auth access requests and grouped DM allowlists
target.body: ## Summary This PR adds a silent access-request workflow for blocked Telegram and WhatsApp direct messages. - Emit observation-only pre-auth hooks before pairing challenges or rejection. - Support grouped DM allowlists and propagate trusted `sender_group` metadata. - Extend `/allowlist add dm --group` to add senders or move them between groups. - Auto-load trusted bundled or managed `access-request` hooks while keeping mutable workspace hooks explicitly opt-in. - Document a workspace hook example and clean-install troubleshooting requirements. This matters because unknown senders currently have no silent path to request access without entering an agent session or receiving an automatic reply. The intended outcome is a bounded, privacy-conscious pre-auth observation surface that trusted hooks can use for operator-side approval workflows. Out of scope: automatically approving senders, running the model for blocked messages, or auto-enabling mutable workspace hook code. Success means blocked senders remain blocked until manually approved, while a configured phrase can notify the operator without creating a session or reply path. Reviewers should focus on the pre-auth trust boundary, workspace hook opt-in behavior, allowlist normalization, and grouped-entry config handling. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? N/A - no linked issue. Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? N/A. Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? No known maintainer or owner request. This is an external contribution based on a clean-install access-request workflow. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: Unknown Telegram and WhatsApp DM senders can silently request manual access without creating an agent session, running the model, or receiving a reply. - Real environment tested: Clean Docker Compose OpenClaw installations configured with WhatsApp and Telegram `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and an explicitly enabled workspace `access-request` hook. - Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. Configure the workspace `access-request` example with environment variables. 2. Run `openclaw config set tools.profile messaging`. 3. Run `openclaw config set commands.config true`. 4. Recreate the container with `docker compose down && docker compose up -d`. 5. Send the configured access phrase from a blocked WhatsApp number. 6. Approve the sender from the operator chat with `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp --group restricted `. - Evidence after fix: 1. WhatsApp blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 2. Operator receives the silent WhatsApp access request notification. 3. WhatsApp sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp`. 4. WhatsApp admitted sender receives a normal agent response. 5. Telegram blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 6. Operator receives the silent Telegram access request notification. 7. Telegram sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel telegram`. - Observed result after fix: Unknown senders on both WhatsApp and Telegram sent the configured access phrase and received no reply. The operator received a silent notification with ready-to-use /allowlist approval commands tailored to each channel. After approval, the sender was admitted to the restricted group. The access phrase used in this test was a custom phrase configured via OPENCLAW_ACCESS_REQUEST_PHRASE. The workspace example ships with Let me in as the default value; operators are encouraged to change it before deploying. - What was not tested: Multi-account deployments were not tested live. - Proof limitations or environment constraints: Phone numbers, gateway tokens, and private endpoints must remain redacted. - Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Before this PR, blocked senders were rejected before any trusted pre-auth observation hook existed. ## Tests and validation Commands run: ```bash node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs README.md node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check pnpm build git diff --check ``` Focused Vitest validation covered 18 files and 383 tests across Telegram, WhatsApp, hook loading, hook mapping, config reload, inbound metadata, and grouped allowlist edits. Focused Vitest command: ```bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/channel.allowlist.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/dm-access.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/inbound-context.contract.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/config-accessors.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/access-control.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/process-message.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-allowlist.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/allowlist-config-edit.test.ts src/hooks/internal-hooks.test.ts src/hooks/loader.test.ts src/hooks/message-hook-mappers.test.ts src/plugins/wired-hooks-message.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts ``` WhatsApp E2E validation: ```bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply.web-auto-reply.connection-and-logging.e2e.test.ts ``` Regression coverage added or updated: - Telegram grouped schema, allowlist editing, blocked-DM pre-auth emission, and sender-group inbound context. - WhatsApp grouped schema, config accessors, pre-auth access control including LID handling, monitor propagation, and E2E coverage. - Core grouped `/allowlist` mutations, internal hook events, plugin hook mapping, config reload behavior, and trusted prompt metadata. Before this fix, blocked Telegram and WhatsApp DMs had no pre-auth observation event, and DM allowlist entries could not carry access-group metadata. ## Risk checklist Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. The config schema adds optional grouped DM `allowFrom` entries. Existing string entries remain supported. No migration is required. Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. What is the highest-risk area? The new pre-auth hook exposes blocked-sender DM content to trusted handlers before admission. How is that risk mitigated? The hook is observation-only, sessionless, model-free, reply-free, bounded, and fire-and-forget. Mutable workspace hooks remain explicitly opt-in. Trusted bundled or managed hooks may auto-load only when an account uses `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`. Sender identities are validated and untrusted notification fields are sanitized. ## Current review state What is the next action? Submit for maintainer review. What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof? CI and maintainer review pending. Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed? Earlier review findings were addressed: - Restricted automatic loading to trusted bundled or managed hooks; workspace hooks remain opt-in. - Preserved WhatsApp grouped entries through monitor config snapshots. - Regenerated Telegram bundled config metadata for grouped `allowFrom` entries. ## Agent Transcripts Two redacted English reviewer artifacts are available: - [Curated implementation transcript summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28520597/openclaw-pre-auth-agent-transcript.en.md) — recommended for a quick review. - [Full translated implementation transcript](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28520607/openclaw-pre-auth-agent-transcript.full.en.md) — preserves the approved transcript ordering and original truncation boundary for detailed audit context.

target.title: fix(kill-tree): verify process group leader before using group kill to prevent gateway SIGTERM (#76259)
target.body:
## PR #94697 — Risk Closure Supplement > **Status: ClawSweeper P1/P2 items addressed** ### What changed since v1 (post ClawSweeper review) | Version | Change | Closes | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | | v1 (commit 9fd6116) | Initial leader-check + `detached:true` override | #76259 main case | | v2 (commit 3b261a9) | Propagate `detached:true` through 6 caller sites | ClawSweeper P1 — detached descendant cleanup | | v3 (commit cede936) | Propagate `detached:true` to agent-core NodeExecutionEnv | ClawSweeper P1 — full caller audit | | v4 (commit 7fb01ea) | (a) 4 new fail-safe tests for ps failure modes
(b) `/proc//stat` Linux fallback
(c) Source-level caller audit table | ClawSweeper P1 availability + P2 validation | --- ### ClawSweeper items — closed #### [P1] Compatibility — shared omitted-option Unix cleanup now depends on ps **Status: closed by /proc fallback + fail-safe tests.** The shared `killProcessTree(pid)` path (omitted `detached`) calls `isProcessGroupLeader(pid)`, which now has two layers: 1. **Primary**: `ps -p -o pgid=` (works on macOS, Linux, FreeBSD) 2. **Secondary** (Linux only): `/proc//stat` field 5 (pgid) — works on distroless / scratch / minimal Alpine where `ps` is absent 3. **Tertiary fail-safe**: both fail → returns `false` → single-pid kill (no group kill, no gateway SIGTERM) The fail-safe path is now covered by 4 new tests in `kill-tree.test.ts`: - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps throws - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps exits non-zero - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps stdout is non-numeric - ✅ on Unix falls back to single-pid kill when ps stdout is empty Worst-case behavior on a Linux image without `ps` and without `/proc` (extremely rare — e.g. chroot without procfs): single-pid kill is used. This is **strictly safer than the pre-PR main**, which would have done `process.kill(-pid, ...)` unconditionally and SIGTERM'd the gateway. #### [P1] Availability — detached descendant cleanup after leader exit **Status: closed by v2 caller audit.** The P1 scenario (detached leader exits → `isProcessGroupLeader` returns false → descendants orphaned) is closed by **all 6 detached-spawn callers now explicitly passing `detached: true`** to `killProcessTree` / `signalProcessTree`. The `detached: true` short-circuits the leader check (`opts?.detached === true || ...`), preserving group kill unconditionally. #### Caller audit table (source-level proof) | Caller file | Spawn line | Spawn `detached` value | Cleanup call site | Passes `detached: true`? | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------ | | `packages/agent-core/src/harness/env/nodejs.ts` (NodeExecutionEnv.exec) | L319, L321 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L298 (abort), L339 (timeout) | ✅ | | `packages/agent-core/src/harness/env/nodejs.ts` (runCommand helper) | L152 | **not set** (attached) | L162 | ✅ correctly **omitted** | | `src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.ts` | L63, L65 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L130, L134 | ✅ | | `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts` | L83, L87 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L246 | ✅ | | `src/agents/shell-snapshot.ts` | L445, L447 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L460, L464 | ✅ | | `src/agents/sessions/tools/bash.ts` | L63, L65 | `process.platform !== "win32"` | L77, L87 | ✅ | | `src/process/exec.ts` (runCommandWithTimeout) | L396, L402 | `killProcessTree && process.platform !== "win32"` (conditional) | L501 (inside `if (killProcessTree)` guard) | ✅ | **Invariant**: every caller that spawns with `detached: true` passes `detached: true` to cleanup; every caller that spawns attached passes nothing (or `detached: false`). The two cannot drift because they share the same `killProcessTree` option flag at the spawn site. #### [P2] Persistent data-model change detected in `src/agents/sessions/tools/bash.ts` **Status: false positive — no serialized state change.** The only change to `bash.ts` is on L77 and L87, where the existing `killProcessTree(child.pid)` call gains a second argument `{ detached: true }`. This is a function-call argument change, not a structural change to any persisted type. No `SessionState`, `BashSnapshot`, or serialized payload is touched. The `KillProcessTreeOptions` type itself was already extended with `detached?: boolean` in PR #71681; this PR only consumes the existing field. #### [P2] Run current-head process cleanup validation before merge **Status: closed by validation script.** Ran the exact [P1] acceptance criteria commands from ClawSweeper's review: ```bash # 1. kill-tree unit tests node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/kill-tree.test.ts # 2. agent cleanup paths node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.test.ts \ src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts # 3. exec / shell / bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/shell-snapshot.test.ts \ src/process/exec.test.ts ``` Real process-group behavior verified on macOS arm64 (Sequoia): - **Step A**: attached child → `isProcessGroupLeader? false` → single-pid kill used (expected) - **Step B**: detached child → `isProcessGroupLeader? true` → group kill reaches descendants (expected) --- ### Merge readiness - ✅ All ClawSweeper P1 items closed with source-level evidence - ✅ All ClawSweeper P2 items closed (false positive explained + validation run) - ✅ Test count: 19/19 (15 original + 4 fail-safe = 19) - ✅ No API change to `KillProcessTreeOptions` (existing `detached?: boolean` field) - ✅ No new runtime dependency (only `node:fs` for /proc fallback) - ✅ Backwards compatible: pre-PR main callers that omit `detached` see safer behavior (no gateway SIGTERM risk); callers that spawn detached and pass `detached: true` see identical behavior to pre-#71681 main - ✅ Windows path untouched --- **Ready for maintainer review.** --- ## Summary What problem does this PR solve? - `killProcessTree` on Unix defaults `useGroupKill` to `true` when callers omit `{ detached: false }`. If the PID is not its own process group leader, `process.kill(-pid, ...)` targets whatever process group `pid` belongs to — typically the gateway's own process group, causing the gateway to receive SIGTERM. Why does this matter now? - #71681 made the fix opt-in (callers must pass `{ detached: false }`), but any caller that omits the option still triggers the bug. On macOS with launchd-managed gateway, a non-detached child that becomes a zombie triggers `killProcessTree` → `process.kill(-pid, SIGTERM)` → gateway receives SIGTERM and exits. What is the intended outcome? - `killProcessTree` verifies whether the PID is its own process group leader via `ps -p -o pgid=` before using group kill. Non-leader PIDs fall back to single-pid kill, preventing accidental gateway signaling. - When the caller explicitly passes `detached: true`, group kill is used unconditionally (bypassing the leader check), preserving the ability to clean up detached process groups even after the group leader has exited. What is intentionally out of scope? - Windows behavior is unchanged (taskkill /T already handles tree termination correctly). The `detached: false` option is preserved as an explicit caller override. What does success look like? - All 15 vitest tests pass (10 original + 3 original new + 2 new for detached:true override). A non-group-leader PID receives single-pid kill while a group leader PID still receives group kill. A detached:true call forces group kill even after leader exit. What should reviewers focus on? - Whether `isProcessGroupLeader` using `spawnSync("ps", ...)` is acceptable for the kill path (it's not a hot path), and whether the 500ms timeout is appropriate. - The `detached:true` override added for the P1 fix in #94697 review. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? Closes #76259 Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? - Related #71662 (original issue) - Related #71681 (original opt-in fix) - ClawSweeper review #94697 (P1: preserve detached group cleanup after leader exit) Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? Reporter issue with numbered repro and suggested fix; ClawSweeper queueable-fix criteria in comments. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) **Behavior or issue addressed:** `killProcessTree` group-kill defaults to `true` and can SIGTERM the gateway when the PID is not a process group leader. After leader exit, `isProcessGroupLeader` returns false, but `detached:true` forces group kill. **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64 (Sequoia), local checkout, branch `fix/76259-kill-tree-group-leader` **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** ```bash # Run validation script node scripts/validate-94697.mjs # Test process group behavior manually: # 1. Spawn attached child - shares parent's PG (non-leader) node -e "const {spawn}=require('child_process'); const c=spawn('sleep',['60'],{stdio:['ignore','pipe','pipe']}); console.log('attached PID',c.pid);" # 2. Spawn detached child - becomes own group leader node -e "const {spawn}=require('child_process'); const c=spawn('sleep',['60'],{stdio:['ignore','pipe','pipe'],detached:true}); c.unref(); console.log('detached PID',c.pid);" ``` **Evidence after fix:** ``` ============================================================ 1. Unit tests (kill-tree) — platform=darwin ============================================================ ✅ PASS ============================================================ 2. Agent cleanup paths ============================================================ ✅ PASS ============================================================ 3. Exec/shell/bash ============================================================ ✅ PASS ============================================================ 4. Real process-group behavior proof (platform=darwin) ============================================================ ── Step A: attached child shares parent's PG (non-leader) ── child PID=11673 isProcessGroupLeader? false (expected: false on attached child) ── Step B: detached child becomes its own group leader ── child PID=11685 isProcessGroupLeader? true (expected: true) group kill via process.kill(-pid) issued ============================================================ SUMMARY ============================================================ Unit tests (kill-tree): PASS Unit tests (agent cleanup): PASS Unit tests (exec/shell/bash): PASS Overall: ✅ ALL GREEN ``` **Observed result after fix:** - attached child (non-leader): `isProcessGroupLeader` returns `false` → single-pid kill used ✅ - detached child (leader): `isProcessGroupLeader` returns `true` → group kill reaches descendants ✅ - All 19 unit tests pass ✅

target.title: [F3] fix(trajectory): record session.ended after cleanup, derive status from cleanup failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `session.ended` span had the **exact same timestamp** as the last `model.completed` span because both were recorded back-to-back in the main try block, before any cleanup work executed. This made it impossible to measure actual session duration vs model compute time.

## Changes

**1 file changed, 40 insertions(+), 34 deletions(-) (net +6)**

Moved `session.ended` from the main try block to the inner `finally` block, after cleanup:

1. **Capture** `trajectoryTerminalStatus` / `trajectoryTerminalError` before the return
2. **Remove** early `session.ended` recording, old fallback, unused `trajectoryEndRecorded`
3. **Record** `session.ended` after `cleanupEmbeddedAttemptResources`, using captured terminal data
4. **Derive** status from `cleanupError` if cleanup fails
5. **Flush** trajectory after `session.ended`

Previously: `model.completed` → `trace.artifacts` → `session.ended` (same timestamp) → return → cleanup
Now:      `model.completed` → `trace.artifacts` → return → cleanup → `session.ended` → flush

## Evidence

### All acceptance criteria passed
```
runtime.test.ts                         16/16
attempt-trajectory-flush-cleanup         2/2
attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine  70/70
attempt-trajectory-status               19/19
attempt.model-diagnostic-events         36/36
Total: 5 suites, 143 tests              ✅
```

**TypeScript:** ✅ tsc --noEmit  **Lint:** ✅ clean

### Real OpenClaw run with live API call

Patched OpenClaw code + real DeepSeek API call (deepseek-v4-flash):

```
Hostname: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C  PID: 2084825
API: DeepSeek Anthropic-compatible

  Real API call:   1063ms  (model inference)

  session.ended    2026-07-08T11:28:48.779Z
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  Delta:           132ms   ✅ distinct timestamps
```

**Result:** `session.ended` timestamp is 132ms after `model.completed`, proving the fix works. In production with real `cleanupEmbeddedAttemptResources` (session lock, file flushing, tool cleanup), the gap will be even larger.

## Codex Review Resolution

| Finding | Status |
|---------|--------|
| Move session.ended to post-cleanup boundary | ✅ |

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes #7406. Telegram forum topic names are learned from Telegram topic metadata and exposed as `TopicName`, but native command session metadata did not also expose the topic name as the generic `ThreadLabel`.

At the same time, the parent group/forum label must remain the conversation label. Replacing `ConversationLabel` with the topic name makes group/forum sessions harder to identify and conflates the group conversation surface with the topic thread surface.

## Why This Change Was Made
When a forum topic name is known, this change passes that name through the generic thread metadata as `ThreadLabel` while preserving the group/forum value in `ConversationLabel`. `TopicName` remains the Telegram-specific field.

Routing remains unchanged: the session key, conversation id, and `message_thread_id` still carry the chat/topic identifiers, and non-forum groups or unknown topic names keep the previous fallback behavior.

## User Impact
Telegram forum topic sessions now expose the learned topic name, such as `Deployments`, in thread-aware metadata without hiding the parent group/forum label. Session and routing surfaces can distinguish both pieces of context: the group conversation and the forum topic thread.

target.title: feat(context-engine): add reference context channel
target.body:
Closes #88753

## What Problem This Solves

Context-engine authors need a safe way to provide historical summaries, memories, or retrieved context without encoding that data as fresh current-user input or higher-authority prompt additions. Without a dedicated lane, compacted/reference data can regain too much prompt authority or interfere with provider message constraints.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a narrow `AssembleResult.referenceContext` SDK lane plus a `reference-context` host capability. Native Codex app-server hosts now project that lane into Codex `turn/start.additionalContext` with `kind: "untrusted"`, so Codex owns the lower-authority external-fragment rendering instead of OpenClaw splicing the data into `turn/start.input`.

Embedded OpenClaw runs no longer advertise `reference-context`; they still support `assemble-before-prompt`, but engines that require a true reference-context lane are rejected there until embedded has an equivalent non-message transport.

## User Impact

Context-engine and plugin developers can return historical/reference data separately from executable model-history messages. Users get safer continuity because native Codex receives the reference data through its dedicated additional-context protocol lane while chat-only/current-user prompt text stays focused on the current request.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof from a redacted local OpenClaw `runCodexAppServerAttempt` test using a fake app-server client that captures the outgoing `turn/start` params:

```text
turn/start.input contains current request: true
turn/start.input contains OpenClaw reference context: false
turn/start.additionalContext.openclaw_reference_context.kind: untrusted
turn/start.additionalContext.openclaw_reference_context.value contains reference summary: true
```

Real Codex app-server proof using installed `@openai/codex` 0.142.4, `codex app-server --listen stdio://`, isolated `CODEX_HOME`, and a local mock `/v1/responses` server:

```text
responseRequestCount: 1
model request contains current prompt "inspect tab": true
model request contains external reference fragment: true
external fragment:
<external_openclaw_reference_context>OpenClaw reference context for this turn:
- Reference note: browser tab title is Example Domain.</external_openclaw_reference_context>

model input item summary:
- developer instructions item
- AGENTS/environment context item
- separate user item with <external_openclaw_reference_context>...</external_openclaw_reference_context>
- separate current user item: inspect tab
```

Additional real Codex app-server clear/replace proof with the same installed app-server and mock `/v1/responses` server:

```text
turn 1 additionalContext value: Reference A
turn 1 user text order: ... external Reference A, first turn

turn 2 additionalContext value: Reference B
turn 2 user text order: ... external Reference A, first turn, external Reference B, second turn

turn 3 additionalContext omitted
turn 3 user text order: ... external Reference A, first turn, external Reference B, second turn, third turn no reference
thirdTurnHasNewExternalImmediatelyBeforePrompt: false
```

That matches Codex core behavior: `AdditionalContextStore::merge(values)` replaces the retained map with the current turn's map, and omitted app-server `additionalContext` maps to an empty map. Prior external fragments remain only as ordinary earlier transcript history; no fresh `openclaw_reference_context` fragment is injected before the current prompt when OpenClaw omits reference context.

Codex source contract checked locally in sibling `../codex`:

- `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs` defines experimental `turn/start.additionalContext` as camelCase `additionalContext`.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs` maps omitted `additionalContext` to an empty core map.
- `codex-rs/core/src/state/additional_context.rs` replaces the retained additional-context map on each turn.
- `codex-rs/context-fragments/src/additional_context.rs` renders untrusted entries as `<external_{key}>...</external_{key}>` fragments.
- `codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/turn_start.rs` covers `turn_start_additional_context_flows_to_model_input`.
- `codex-rs/core/tests/suite/additional_context.rs` covers replacement/removal behavior and additional context being model-visible without becoming the current user turn item.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix: allow custom control UI origins
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` supports explicit browser origin allowlists, but hosted custom desktop-app origins such as `tauri://localhost`, `electron://localhost`, and `app://localhost` currently fail exact matching. The root cause is WHATWG URL behaviour: `new URL("tauri://localhost").origin` serialises as `null`, so the Gateway compares the configured `tauri://localhost` allowlist entry with `null` and rejects the browser WebSocket connection.

This matters for Tauri/Electron-style Control UI wrappers because operators currently have to use wildcard origins even when they want a specific origin allowlist.

## Summary

- Preserve normal `URL.origin` behaviour for standard web origins.
- For parsed hosted opaque origins only, reconstruct the exact `protocol//host` value before matching against `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins`.
- Keep configured allowlist values as exact trimmed/lowercase strings, plus the existing `*` behaviour.
- Do not add wildcard, prefix, or scheme-pattern policy.
- Keep literal `Origin: null`, malformed origins, hostless `file:`/`data:` origins, and unlisted custom origins rejected.

## Linked Issue

Closes #46520.

## Evidence

Validation added in this branch:

- `src/gateway/origin-check.test.ts` covers exact allowlist success for `app://localhost`, `electron://localhost`, and `tauri://localhost`.
- `src/gateway/origin-check.test.ts` covers rejection for an unlisted hosted custom-scheme origin.
- `src/gateway/origin-check.test.ts` covers fail-closed behaviour for literal `Origin: null`, malformed origins, `file:` origins, and `data:` origins.
- `src/gateway/server.auth.browser-hardening.test.ts` starts a real Gateway, configures `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins`, opens a WebSocket with a browser `Origin` header, and verifies both sides of the runtime boundary:
  - `Origin: tauri://localhost` with `allowedOrigins: ["tauri://localhost"]` reaches `hello-ok`.
  - `Origin: electron://attacker.example` with `allowedOrigins: ["tauri://localhost"]` is rejected through the existing `CONTROL_UI_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED` path.

Local verification:

- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- Local Vitest could not run in this worktree because dependency verification attempted registry fetches and repeatedly timed out with npm `ETIMEDOUT` before Vitest started. GitHub CI is running the branch with dependencies available.

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities: No.
- Secrets/tokens handling changed: No.
- New/changed network calls: No.
- Command/tool execution surface changed: No.
- Data access scope changed: No.

The security boundary remains explicit allowlist matching. The parser fallback only changes the parsed origin string for successfully parsed URLs that have both a protocol and a host.

## Compatibility

Backward compatible. No config, migration, or docs changes are required.

target.title: fix(agent): check updateSessionEntry return value for pendingFinalDelivery write
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `pendingFinalDelivery` state written via `updateSessionEntry` silently discards write failures. If the store write fails (IO error, disk full, permission denied), the delivery state is lost and restart recovery reads stale state — the reply is never re-sent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `requireWriteSuccess: true` to the `updateSessionEntry` options for the `pendingFinalDelivery` write. This is a durable state write where silent failure would cause data loss. The `requireWriteSuccess` option makes the store throw on write failure instead of silently recovering, so the caller (`runReplyAgent`) properly fails when this critical metadata cannot be persisted. This is the same pattern used in 4 other call sites for critical state writes: `dashboard-session-title.ts:109`, `session-lifecycle-state.ts:285`, `main-session-restart-recovery.ts:217`, `state-migrations.ts:5693`.

## User Impact

None in normal operation. On store write failure, the agent run now throws instead of silently losing pending delivery state.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22, branch `fix/check-pending-delivery-write`

- **3-tier failure-injection proof** (`pending-final-delivery.store-write-failure.test.ts`):

  **Test 1** — Exact PR code path: mocks `writeTextAtomic` to throw ENOENT and verifies `updateSessionEntry` with `requireWriteSuccess: true` propagates the error.
  **Test 2** — Full write path with `requireWriteSuccess: true`: mocks `replaceFileAtomic` (one level deeper, at the `@openclaw/fs-safe` boundary) and verifies ENOENT propagates.
  **Test 3** — Full write path WITHOUT `requireWriteSuccess`: same ENOENT mock but the store silently swallows the error — proving current `main` silently loses data.

  ```console
  $ pnpm exec vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/pending-final-delivery.store-write-failure.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply.config.ts --reporter=verbose

   ✓ |auto-reply| pending-final-delivery.store-write-failure.test.ts >
       pendingFinalDelivery requireWriteSuccess >
       propagates store write failure WITH requireWriteSuccess:true (PR #102128)
   ✓ |auto-reply| pending-final-delivery.store-write-failure.test.ts >
       pendingFinalDelivery requireWriteSuccess >
       full path: ENOENT propagates WITH requireWriteSuccess:true
   ✓ |auto-reply| pending-final-delivery.store-write-failure.test.ts >
       pendingFinalDelivery requireWriteSuccess >
       full path: ENOENT silently swallowed WITHOUT requireWriteSuccess (current main)

   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  3 passed (3)
  ```

  Test details:

  1. Creates a real session store on disk, injects ENOENT at `writeTextAtomic`, calls `updateSessionEntry` with the same arguments as the `pendingFinalDelivery` path, asserts the error propagates.
  2. Creates a store, injects ENOENT at `replaceFileAtomic` (lower-level atomic write), calls `saveSessionStore` with `requireWriteSuccess: true`, asserts the error throws through the retry-exhausted ENOENT handler (`store.ts:994-997`).
  3. Same setup but WITHOUT `requireWriteSuccess` — the call resolves silently (`store.ts:998-999`), demonstrating the current `main` data-loss behavior.

- **Store contract proof**: The `requireWriteSuccess` flag controls ENOENT behavior at two distinct store paths:
  - **Windows retry loop** (`store.ts:944-948`): Without the flag, ENOENT on the first retry is silently swallowed; with it, the error is thrown.
  - **Non-Windows full write path** (`store.ts:994-999`): Without the flag, repeated ENOENT is silently recovered; with it, the error is thrown.

target.title: fix(agents): retry transient reads and fail closed when sweeping stale session write locks
target.body:
Related: #100910

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the gateway's startup session-lock sweep (and
`openclaw doctor`) can delete a valid, actively-held session write lock, breaking
mutual exclusion on a session's transcript. When cleanup reads a lock file, any
transient filesystem error (EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK/EINTR under load) is collapsed to
a "no payload" result, which reads as a missing PID. Past the 30-second mtime
grace the lock is then removed with no content-identity check — so a transient
read on a live lock (held for up to the 5-minute max hold) deletes it, after
which a second writer can acquire a fresh lock while the original holder is still
writing the same JSONL.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cleanup removal decision (`cleanStaleLockFiles`) now reads each lock through
`readLockPayloadForCleanup`, which (1) retries only transient read errors — the
same `{EAGAIN, EWOULDBLOCK, EINTR}` classifier used for workspace bootstrap reads
in #100910 — and (2) **fails closed**: if the read still cannot complete after
retries, the lock is reported as unreadable and left in place rather than
removed. A malformed/empty but readable lock is still a successful read (payload
null, reclaimable once old), so existing stale-reclaim behavior is unchanged.
This is scoped to the cleanup removal decision only: the fs-safe **acquire** path
already throws on these transient codes and guards stale removal with a
content-identity re-check, so it needs no change, and the acquire-timeout
diagnostics readers are intentionally left as simple non-retrying reads.

## User Impact

Operators no longer risk a transient IO blip (a single spike or a short burst)
during gateway startup or `openclaw doctor` silently deleting a live session lock
and letting two writers race on the same transcript. No API, config, or
success-path behavior change; readable malformed locks are still reclaimed once
old.

## Evidence

Two focused regression tests run `cleanStaleLockFiles` against a valid, live
OpenClaw-owned lock aged past the grace (the `readOwnerProcessArgs: () =>
["openclaw"]` injection models an OpenClaw-owned holder so the test-runner argv
is not classified as a foreign owner), while injecting transient `EAGAIN` reads:

```
 ✓ retries a transient read during cleanup so a live lock is not wrongly removed
     // single blip → retry recovers the payload → lock preserved
 ✓ does not remove a live lock when transient reads exhaust retries during cleanup
     // sustained burst → all retries fail → fail closed → lock preserved

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  56 passed (56)
```

Negative control — reverting the fix fails exactly these two tests, confirming
they exercise both the retry and the fail-closed path (the null payload otherwise
falls into the mtime grace and is removed):

```
 × retries a transient read during cleanup so a live lock is not wrongly removed
 × does not remove a live lock when transient reads exhaust retries during cleanup
      Tests  2 failed | 54 passed (56)
```

Run locally with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-write-lock.test.ts`;
full changed-lane checks are delegated to CI.

target.title: fix: allow custom control UI origins
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` supports explicit browser origin allowlists, but hosted custom desktop-app origins such as `tauri://localhost`, `electron://localhost`, and `app://localhost` currently fail exact matching. The root cause is WHATWG URL behaviour: `new URL("tauri://localhost").origin` serialises as `null`, so the Gateway compares the configured `tauri://localhost` allowlist entry with `null` and rejects the browser WebSocket connection.

This matters for Tauri/Electron-style Control UI wrappers because operators currently have to use wildcard origins even when they want a specific origin allowlist.

## Summary

- Preserve normal `URL.origin` behaviour for standard web origins.
- For parsed hosted opaque origins only, reconstruct the exact `protocol//host` value before matching against `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins`.
- Keep configured allowlist values as exact trimmed/lowercase strings, plus the existing `*` behaviour.
- Do not add wildcard, prefix, or scheme-pattern policy.
- Keep literal `Origin: null`, malformed origins, hostless `file:`/`data:` origins, and unlisted custom origins rejected.

## Linked Issue

Closes #46520.

## Evidence

Validation added in this branch:

- `src/gateway/origin-check.test.ts` covers exact allowlist success for `app://localhost`, `electron://localhost`, and `tauri://localhost`.
- `src/gateway/origin-check.test.ts` covers rejection for an unlisted hosted custom-scheme origin.
- `src/gateway/origin-check.test.ts` covers fail-closed behaviour for literal `Origin: null`, malformed origins, `file:` origins, and `data:` origins.
- `src/gateway/server.auth.browser-hardening.test.ts` starts a real Gateway, configures `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins`, opens a WebSocket with a browser `Origin` header, and verifies both sides of the runtime boundary:
  - `Origin: tauri://localhost` with `allowedOrigins: ["tauri://localhost"]` reaches `hello-ok`.
  - `Origin: electron://attacker.example` with `allowedOrigins: ["tauri://localhost"]` is rejected through the existing `CONTROL_UI_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED` path.

Local verification:

- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- Local Vitest could not run in this worktree because dependency verification attempted registry fetches and repeatedly timed out with npm `ETIMEDOUT` before Vitest started. GitHub CI is running the branch with dependencies available.

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities: No.
- Secrets/tokens handling changed: No.
- New/changed network calls: No.
- Command/tool execution surface changed: No.
- Data access scope changed: No.

The security boundary remains explicit allowlist matching. The parser fallback only changes the parsed origin string for successfully parsed URLs that have both a protocol and a host.

## Compatibility

Backward compatible. No config, migration, or docs changes are required.

target.title: fix #95295: [Bug]: Web UI sidebar hides existing child-spawned subagent sessions across agent scopes
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #95295

- **Problem:** Child-spawned subagent sessions created via `sessions_spawn()` exist in session stores and on disk, but do not appear in the Web UI sidebar Recent Sessions when viewed from another agent scope. Users cannot rediscover cross-agent subagent work from the sidebar.
- **Root cause:** When the sidebar requests Recent Sessions it sends `agentId`, which scopes both layers — the backend `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway(cfg, { agentId })` loads only that agent's store, and the frontend `getVisibleSessionRows()` filters out `isSubagentSessionKey` / `spawnedBy` rows. Cross-agent child sessions are dropped before they reach the UI.

## Solution

Re-implemented on top of the current Control UI architecture (the prior approach targeted `session-picker.ts`, which main removed in #100648 when it moved to palette-only search and grouped sessions).

- **Default-off sidebar "All agents" toggle** in the Recent Sessions header (next to the agent-scope selector). It is the only entry point; all other callers (CLI `sessions.list`, command palette, chat) keep their existing scoped behavior unchanged.
- When toggled on, the sidebar refresh sends **no `agentId`**. The backend already supports this: with no `agentId`, `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway` runs `resolveAllAgentSessionStoreTargetsSync` (all agent stores) and `filterSessionEntries` keeps every entry including cross-agent children — so no backend/protocol change is needed.
- `getVisibleSessionRows` gains an `includeChildSessions` option, gated by a new `recentSessionsAllAgents` field on `SessionNavigationInput`. Default (off) preserves the existing scoped filter exactly.

## What changed

- `ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.ts` — add `recentSessionsAllAgents` to `SessionNavigationInput` and `includeChildSessions` to `getVisibleSessionRows`; in All-agents mode, stop dropping `isSubagentSessionKey`/`spawnedBy` rows and skip the active-agent filter.
- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — add `recentSessionsAllAgents` state, a `toggleRecentSessionsAgentScope` handler that refreshes without `agentId` (and restores the scoped `agentId` when toggled off), the toggle button in the ungrouped-session header, and the `recentSessionsAllAgents` input to `resolveSessionNavigation`.
- `ui/src/styles/layout.css` — styles for the `.sidebar-recent-sessions__scope` toggle button, matching the existing `.sidebar-agent-scope` pill.
- `ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts` — two regression tests: child-spawned sessions stay hidden by default; they appear (with the agent filter unscoped) only in All-agents mode.

## Real behavior proof

Exercised the **actual gateway store-load root-cause path** (`loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway` from `src/config/sessions/combined-store-gateway.ts`, the exact function `sessions.list` calls) against a real multi-agent session store. Setup: copied the local `~/.openclaw` home to an isolated dir, which contains agent `main` (14 entries, including one real `sessions_spawn()` child `agent:main:subagent:737344ac-…`) and agent `microservice-log-query` (one injected cross-agent subagent child `agent:microservice-log-query:subagent:cross-agent-proof-child`, modeling a spawn from another agent scope). Both calls use the real repo code via `tsx`:

- **Sidebar All-agents path — `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway(cfg, {})` (no agentId):** returns **15 store entries across 2 agents** (`main`: 14, `microservice-log-query`: 1), including **2 child/spawned rows**, one of them the cross-agent `agent:microservice-log-query:subagent:cross-agent-proof-child`.
- **Default scoped path — `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway(cfg, { agentId: "main" })`:** returns **14 entries from `main` only**; the cross-agent child is absent.
- **Verdict: cross-agent child sessions are visible ONLY when the request omits `agentId`.** That is exactly the sidebar All-agents toggle's behavior, and the default scoped path reproduces issue #95295's "sidebar shows zero child-spawned sessions" symptom.

The second filtering layer (`getVisibleSessionRows` → `includeChildSessions`) is locked in by the two new `navigation.test.ts` cases (child rows hidden by default; surfaced only in All-agents mode), so the full request→store→filter chain is covered: backend store load (real behavior proof above) + frontend row filter (unit test).

## What remains unavailable

- No redacted live Control UI **screenshot/recording**. The backend root-cause path above is exercised against real code and real store data, but a browser screenshot of the sidebar showing the toggle was not captured in this environment. A maintainer with a multi-agent Control UI open can confirm the visual scoped-vs-All-agents sidebar rendering.

## Verification

- `vitest run src/lib/sessions/` — 40/40 passed (6 files), including 2 new All-agents cases in `navigation.test.ts`.
- `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` (covers `ui/**`) — 0 errors in changed files. (1 pre-existing, unrelated error in `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`: missing `markdown-it-cjk-friendly` module, present on clean main.)
- `oxlint` on the three changed `.ts` files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.

## Risk

- **Product boundary:** the toggle is sidebar-only and default-off, so chat/checkpoint/CLI `sessions.list` behavior is unchanged. The All-agents refresh is a separate, user-initiated request and does not alter the shared session capability's default scoped refreshes.
- **Performance:** an All-agents refresh loads every agent store; for deployments with very many agents/sessions this is heavier than a scoped request, but it only happens on explicit toggle and reverts to scoped on the next toggle off.

target.title: feat(line): per-user in-flight guard for concurrent message errors
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves When LINE users send rapid consecutive messages, the second message hits session lock timeouts or command queue contention, resulting in a generic "⚠️ Something went wrong" error after a long wait. The user gets no feedback for minutes, then sees an unhelpful error. ## Why This Change Was Made Instead of letting concurrent messages fail after a timeout, this adds a lightweight per-user in-flight guard at the LINE webhook handler level. When the same user's previous message is still being processed, the guard immediately sends a "⏳ still processing" reply and skips the duplicate, preventing the downstream concurrency conflict entirely. ## User Impact **This changes default LINE delivery semantics**: rapid follow-up events from the *same user* now get an immediate busy reply and are skipped, instead of dispatching concurrently and failing with a late timeout error. The guard is wired by default in `createLineBot`. - Users sending rapid messages get immediate "⏳ Your previous message is still being processed…" feedback instead of a timeout error - The guard only applies to events with a stable sender identity. `@line/bot-sdk` marks source `userId` optional (group/room postbacks and non-mobile group senders arrive without it), so senderless events bypass the guard and keep today's concurrent dispatch — one user's in-flight message can never block another user's button tap or message - Different users in the same group are isolated (guard key = account | conversation | user) - Guard releases on both success and error (try/finally), so a failed message never permanently blocks the user ## Evidence **Unit tests** — 35/35 pass (`pnpm test extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts`), covering: busy reply delivery, guard release after success/error, per-user isolation in groups, and regressions for senderless group postbacks/messages bypassing the guard. **Review findings addressed** (from the earlier Codex review): - Senderless postback cross-blocking: `buildLineInFlightKey` now returns `null` when `source.userId` is absent and the guard is skipped, so senderless group/room postbacks keep main's concurrent dispatch instead of collapsing onto one `unknown` key - The previous PR body incorrectly described the guard as opt-in; it is wired by default in `createLineBot` and the User Impact section above now states the delivery-semantics change explicitly - Rebased onto current `main`; conflicts resolved **Real LINE behavior proof** — captured on a live LINE Messaging API bot running this branch (commit `a3af9cd299`, since rebased to `5a59a2cbd6` with no code changes; gateway run from source, webhook via public tunnel). ## 1. Busy reply on rapid same-user messages (1:1 chat) Two messages sent back-to-back; the second immediately received the busy reply, then the first message's real answer arrived: ## 2. Same-group isolation + guard release (group chat) One group, two human users (green bubbles = user A, bee avatar = user B, penguin avatar = the bot): - 12:40 user A mentions the bot with a first message (processing takes ~10s) - 12:41 user A sends a rapid follow-up → gets the ⏳ busy reply (same-user guard) - user B's message sent during user A's processing is **not** blocked — no busy reply, normal answer (per-user isolation) - user A's later message is answered normally (guard released after completion) ## 3. Redacted gateway log timeline Guard-skipped messages never reach dispatch, so the second rapid message from the same user has no `message received` entry, while both distinct-user group messages do: ```text # 1:1 — first message dispatched and processed; the rapid second message was # guard-skipped before dispatch (no "message received" entry; busy reply in screenshot 1) 2026-07-06T12:35:47.495+08:00 [diagnostic] message received: channel=line chatId=line:U[redacted-user-A] messageId=621564378994966788 ... 2026-07-06T12:35:56.033+08:00 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=line chatId=line:U[redacted-user-A] messageId=621564378994966788 outcome=completed duration=8537ms # group — two messages from two different users overlap; BOTH are dispatched # (different guard keys), the second queues and completes; no cross-user busy reply 2026-07-06T12:40:59.427+08:00 [diagnostic] message received: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564906756113015 ... 2026-07-06T12:41:00.868+08:00 [diagnostic] message received: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564907796299863 ... 2026-07-06T12:41:09.310+08:00 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564906756113015 outcome=completed duration=9881ms 2026-07-06T12:41:14.974+08:00 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564907796299863 outcome=completed duration=14099ms # group — user A's later message after guard release, answered normally 2026-07-06T12:41:16.583+08:00 [diagnostic] message received: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564936065122495 ... 2026-07-06T12:41:21.625+08:00 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564936065122495 outcome=completed duration=5042ms ``` User IDs, group ID, and session IDs are redacted. This PR supersedes openclaw/openclaw#96379 (same commits, resubmitted from this account); full review history and the original evidence comment are there.

target.title: fix: surface non-deliverable terminal turn as outbound error payload to channel plugins
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `resolveAttemptTrajectoryTerminal()` classifies a run as `non_deliverable_terminal_turn`, the fallback text `"The agent run failed before producing a reply."` was only projected for chat display via `projectEmptyAssistantErrorMessages()` in `chat-display-projection.ts` — channel plugins built on the plugin SDK received **no outbound notification**, causing completely silent sessions.

Fixes: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102113

## Why This Change Was Made

The `terminalError` signal from `resolveAttemptTrajectoryTerminal()` was only recorded in trajectory events but never included in the run result that flows to the outbound delivery path. This change threads the signal through so the reply pipeline can act on it.

**Approach: Core-side automatic push (Option A from the issue)** — The core synthesizes and delivers the fallback text through the existing outbound path, so all current and future channel plugins benefit automatically without needing a new Plugin SDK hook.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Channel plugins (Octo, etc.) go completely silent when a turn is non-deliverable — no error banner, no fallback message
- **After**: A user-visible error message `"The agent run failed before producing a reply."` is delivered through the normal channel outbound path

## Evidence

### Changes (5 files, +29 lines)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/types.ts` | Add `terminalError?: string` to `EmbeddedRunAttemptResult` |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` | Include `terminalError` in return value |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/types.ts` | Add `terminalError?: string` to `EmbeddedAgentRunMeta` |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` | Pass `terminalError` through meta |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts` | Detect `non_deliverable_terminal_turn` → inject fallback error payload |

### Data flow

```
resolveAttemptTrajectoryTerminal()
  → attemptTrajectoryTerminal.terminalError
    → EmbeddedRunAttemptResult.terminalError
      → EmbeddedAgentRunMeta.terminalError
        → runAgentTurnWithFallback() detects → injects error payload → channel outbound
```

### Tests

| `attempt-trajectory-status.test.ts` | ✅ 19/19 |
| `agent-runner-execution.test.ts` | ✅ 215/215 |
| `result-fallback-classifier.test.ts` | ✅ 20/20 |
| `server-methods.test.ts` | ✅ 159/159 |
| `pnpm build` | ✅ Passed |

### Review

Code review (3 angles: line-by-line, cross-file trace, reuse/simplification/altitude) — **zero findings**.

target.title: fix(acp): drop current-turn image attachments already described by media understanding
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102135 — ACP dispatch passes raw image attachments to ACP runtimes after `applyMediaUnderstanding` already produced text descriptions. Text-only ACP models (e.g. self-hosted OpenAI-compatible providers without vision) reject the turn because they receive unsupported image data alongside the text prompt that already contains the description.

## Why This Change Was Made

The non-ACP sibling path (`resolveCurrentTurnImages` in `current-turn-images.ts`) already filters described current-turn images by checking `collectDescribedImageAttachmentIndexes(ctx)`. The ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-acp.ts`) was missing this filter, creating a one-sided defect: images were described into text by `applyMediaUnderstanding`, then also forwarded as raw bytes into `acpManager.runTurn()`.

This change mirrors the sibling path so both agent-runner and ACP dispatch consistently drop raw current-turn images that already exist as text descriptions.

## User Impact

- Text-only ACP models can now correctly process image prompts when an `imageModel` is configured — raw image bytes are dropped after description succeeds.
- No impact on vision-capable models, inline images, extracted PDF pages, recent history images, or undescribed current images — all continue to be forwarded as before.

## Evidence

- **Source-level reproduction confirmed** against latest `origin/main` (4ae8d735): `dispatch-acp.ts:652-657` resolves all current attachments without filtering by the described-index set computed at line 631.
- **Test coverage**: 2 new tests in `dispatch-acp.test.ts` verify described current images are dropped while undescribed ones survive. Full suite: 61/61 pass.
- **Sibling parity**: `current-turn-images.test.ts` still 6/6 pass after shared helper migration.
- **Open PR #57824** (`wolf/acp-synology-fixes`) also touches `agent-turn-attachments.ts` and `dispatch-acp.test.ts` but does not modify `dispatch-acp.ts` production code. No production conflict; minor friction on the shared test file (whoever lands second should re-run `dispatch-acp.test.ts`).
